# Opening the reader, system pages and other apps; keeping awake, downloading and switching orientation

This guide covers taking the user elsewhere, plus a few common device abilities: handing a book to the system reader (2.20), listing every book on the card and getting covers (2.33), opening cloud sync, the font page and keyboard dictionaries (2.27), opening another app (2.32), sleep, power off and full refresh (2.32), keeping the device awake (2.18), saving a download straight to a file (2.18), and switching orientation during a session (2.18). The full rules are in sections 25, 22, 13, 14 and 3 of the specification.

## Handing a book to the reader (2.20)

After a book-source or download app has saved an epub or txt into the app folder, it does not need its own reading screen: `ctx.system:open("file", ...)` hands it to the system reader. Reading progress, recent reading and reading statistics behave as if the user had opened the file from the file manager, and when the user comes back from the reader they return to your app (as a new session).

![A bookshelf picks its buttons with can_open; a recipe board stays awake and rotates to landscape in the session](/docs/reader/open-rotate-en.webp)

```lua
local function read_now(ctx, name)
  if not ctx.system:can_open("file", { name = name }) then
    ctx.dialog:toast("Cannot open this file")
    return
  end
  ctx.system:open("file", { name = name })   -- ends this session after the current callback returns
end
```

- **File**: `name` is a file name directly inside `AppFiles/<app_id>/`, never a path. 2.20 can open `epub`, `txt`, `xtc`, `xtch` and `xtcz`; `.xtapp` files and files without an extension cannot be opened.
- **Book**: `ctx.system:open("book", { id = book.id })` opens a book given by `ctx.reader:books()` or `current()`. It needs the `reader` permission; a book that appears only in `all_books()` is not recognised. A 2.33 package also accepts books from `library()`; see the next section.
- `open` takes effect after the current callback returns and calls `on_leave`, so save your state to `ctx.state` before calling it. You cannot choose a chapter or page.
- Check with `can_open(target, opts)` first: it is false when the file is missing, the extension has no reader, there is no storage card, or the session is a lock-screen session. `open` then returns `nil, "not_found"`, `nil, "not_supported"` or `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- Without `opts`, `can_open("file")` answers whether this device supports the target at all. On an older device it is false; degrade on that, not on `ctx.api.minor`.

## Listing every book on the card and getting covers (2.33)

`books()` only returns the 18 most recently read books. When a bookshelf or bookstore app needs every book on the storage card, including books never opened, use `ctx.reader:library(opts)`. It pages through the books in the system bookshelf's "All" view. It needs the `reader` permission and a manifest `api` of at least `"2.33"`; in older packages `ctx.reader.library` is nil.

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.33", "permissions": ["reader"]
local PAGE = 20

local function load_page(ctx, page)
  local r, err = ctx.reader:library({ offset = page * PAGE, limit = PAGE, sort = "title" })
  if not r then
    if err == "busy" then   -- the bookshelf is still indexing after the card was inserted; try again shortly
      ctx:after(3000, function(ctx) load_page(ctx, page) end)
    end
    status = err
    return
  end
  total, books = r.total, r.books
  ctx:invalidate()
end

-- The user picked a book: even one never opened can go straight to the reader
ctx.system:open("book", { id = books[i].id })
```

- **Options** (all optional): `offset` starts at 0; `limit` is 1–50, default 20; `sort` is `"recent"` (default, books read first), `"added"`, `"title"`, `"author"` or `"size"`; `status` is `"all"`, `"unread"`, `"reading"` or `"finished"`; `format` is `"all"`, `"epub"`, `"txt"` or `"xtc"` (which includes `xtch` and `xtcz`).
- **Result** `{ total, books }`: `total` is the number of books matching the filters and does not change between pages; when `offset` is not less than `total`, `books` is an empty table. Each book has `id`, `title`, `author`, `format`, `status`, `percent`, `size`, `added` (may be nil), `file` and `has_cover`.
- The data comes from the system bookshelf's index; the card is not scanned on each call. A book the user has just copied appears once the index is updated.
- **Errors**: `nil, "busy"` while the first index is built after inserting the card (try again later); `nil, "not_found"` with no storage card; `nil, "invalid_argument"` for bad option values; `nil, "out_of_memory"` when memory runs out.
- `library()` is read-only: it does not generate covers and does not change the bookshelf's sorting or filters.
- For a 2.33 package, `ctx.system:open("book", ...)` also accepts ids from `library()`; if the book file has been deleted it returns `nil, "not_found"`.

**Covers.** `cover(id)` only returns covers the system has already generated, so a book never shown on the bookshelf has none. From 2.33 you can pass `source = "epub"` to read the cover image straight from the EPUB file:

```lua
local img, err = ctx.reader:cover(book.id, { source = "epub", max_w = 160, max_h = 240 })
if img then covers[book.id] = img end   -- keep it once you have it; do not fetch it every frame
```

- EPUB only: other formats return `nil, "not_supported"`; a book with no cover image returns `nil, "not_found"`. `has_cover` being true does not guarantee a cover.
- `max_w` and `max_h` shrink the image proportionally (default: the screen size); `gray` works as in `ctx.image:decode`. An unsupported, damaged or oversized image returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- Each call opens the book file, so it is slow. When a screen needs many covers, fetch them over several frames.
- Covers are runtime images: at most 8 at a time per session, 524288 bytes in total; beyond that you get `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. When paging, call `img:release()` on covers no longer shown.
- The result is not written to the system cover cache. Packages for 2.0–2.32 that pass `opts` have it ignored, the same as `cover(id)`.

## Opening cloud sync, the font page and keyboard dictionaries (2.27)

When the app is missing something, it can take the user straight to the right system page: cloud sync when nothing has been pushed yet, the font page to change fonts, or the dictionary download when composed input lacks a dictionary. When the user comes back from that page, they return to your app (as a new session).

```lua
-- The user tapped "Go to cloud sync"
local function go_sync(ctx)
  if ctx.system:can_open("cloud.sync") then
    ctx.state.page = "inbox"          -- open ends the session, so save where to come back to
    ctx.system:open("cloud.sync")
  end
end
```

| Target | Page opened |
| --- | --- |
| `"cloud.sync"` | Cloud sync: the sync list when bound, the binding page when not |
| `"settings.font"` | The font page in the toolbox settings, where the user picks the TTF used by apps |
| `"settings.keyboard_dict"` | System settings "General → Keyboard → Download dictionaries", the dictionaries composed input needs |

- No permission and no manifest change are needed; packages for 2.0–2.26 can use them too. Check host support with `can_open(target)`, not `ctx.api.minor`: it is true in a normal session and false in a lock-screen session or when the device lacks the page.
- `opts` is ignored; you cannot choose anything inside the page. When unsupported or in a lock-screen session, `open` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- Call it only after an explicit user action. Do not jump away automatically when a push succeeds or a download finishes; it interrupts what the user is doing.
- If the user opens a downloaded book or app from the cloud sync list, that item opens by the page's own rules and does not return to your app.

## Opening another app (2.32)

Home-screen, launcher and folder apps can open another installed app with `ctx.system:open("app", ...)`. When that app ends, the user returns to your app (as a new session). It needs the `apps` permission and an `api` of at least `"2.32"`; take the `id` from `ctx.apps:list()` or `recent()`, see "Installed apps: building home screens and launchers".

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.32", "permissions": ["apps"]
local function launch(ctx, id)
  if not ctx.system:can_open("app", { id = id }) then
    ctx.dialog:toast("This app cannot be opened")
    return
  end
  ctx.system:open("app", { id = id, open = { page = "today" } })
end
```

- **Session**: after the current callback returns, this session ends (`on_leave` is called) and the target app opens.
- **Coming back**: when the target calls `ctx:quit()`, leaves the back key unhandled, is force-quit with a long press on back, or ends with an error, the user returns to your app. Going home with the system key, locking or powering off does not return. Only one level of origin is kept: if the target opens a third app, the third app returns to the target.
- **What the target receives**: its `ctx.launch` for that session is `{ source = "app", from = "<your app_id>", open = ... }`. `open` is passed through unchanged and must encode to at most 191 bytes; without it the field is absent.
- **Errors**: no `apps` permission, a lock-screen session, a missing or empty `id`, your own `id`, or an `open` that is not a table or is too long return `nil, "invalid_argument"`; an app that is not installed returns `nil, "not_found"`; an `outdated` target, or one whose `requires` this device does not meet, returns `nil, "not_supported"`. `can_open` is false in all of these cases.
- `can_open("app")` without `opts` is true in a normal session with the `apps` permission; use it to check whether the host implements 2.32.

## Sleep, power off and full refresh (2.32)

`ctx.system:act(name)` asks the system to do something the user can already do with a hardware key or the system menu. It needs no permission, and packages for 2.0–2.31 can use it too.

```lua
function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.phase == "up" and hit(sleep_btn, ev) then
    local ok, err = ctx.system:act("sleep")   -- only during a user action
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

| `name` | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `"sleep"` | Lock the screen, the same as a short press on the power key: ends this session (`on_leave` is called) and the device sleeps |
| `"power_off"` | Power off. The system first shows a confirmation (the app gets `on_pause` and `on_resume`); if the user cancels, they return to your app |
| `"refresh"` | One full refresh on the next frame, the same as `ctx:invalidate("full")` |

- `"sleep"` and `"power_off"` work only inside an `on_input` that delivers a key `up` or pointer `up` (including functions it calls directly). From timers, `on_load`, `on_tick`, network completions and other callbacks they return `nil, "inactive"`: sleeping and powering off are the user's decision. `"refresh"` has no such restriction.
- Other errors: an unknown `name` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`; a lock-screen session returns `nil, "inactive"`; while the power-off confirmation is showing it returns `nil, "busy"`; a `name` that is not a string raises a Lua error.
- Save your state to `ctx.state` before `"sleep"`; like `open`, it ends the session.
- Leave refreshing to the system and do not call `"refresh"` on a timer; use it only when the user taps a button such as "Refresh screen".
- Use `ctx.frontlight` for the front light and `ctx.screen:set_orientation` above for orientation; `act` does not duplicate them.

## Timers and dashboards: keeping awake (2.18)

Timers, recipe steps and dashboards are "in use but not touched", and the system's automatic power-off would interrupt them after a few minutes. `ctx.device:keep_awake(ms)` stops the system from powering off because of idleness for `ms` milliseconds.

```lua
local function on_tick(ctx)
  -- Renew 10 minutes at a time: valid while the app runs, gone when it exits
  ctx.device:keep_awake(10 * 60 * 1000)
end
```

- `ms` is an integer from 0 to 14400000 (4 hours); 0 cancels. Each call restarts the timer from the moment of the call and does not add up; to go longer, call again shortly before it expires.
- It only postpones, never brings forward: a value shorter than the system's remaining idle time does not power the device off earlier.
- It only stops idle power-off. The power key still locks or turns off the device; below 5% battery and not charging it does not hold.
- It lasts only for this session: exiting, going home, entering the lock screen or an error ends it at once. In a lock-screen session it returns `nil, "inactive"`.
- A device that stays on uses more power, so say so in the description of an app that keeps renewing. The Studio preview has no automatic power-off and only records the last value.

## Downloading large files: save to a file (2.18)

When downloading a novel or a large JSON, do not put the whole response into `res.body`. Set `save` on `ctx.net:request` and the host writes the body directly into the app folder, which you then read in parts.

```lua
ctx.net:request({
  url = "https://example.com/books/three-body.txt",
  save = { to = "files", name = "three-body.txt" },
  timeout_ms = 60000,
}, function(ctx, res)
  if res.saved then
    -- Download finished: hand it straight to the reader
    ctx.system:open("file", { name = "three-body.txt" })
  end
end)
```

- `timeout_ms` is an integer from 1000 to 60000, default 30000, and covers the whole time from the call until the response is complete. Devices up to 2.17 ignore it and use a fixed limit of 30000 ms.
- `res.saved` is true when the file was replaced; it is nil when `save` was not set.
- From 2.18, `method` can also be `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, and `PROPFIND`, `PROPPATCH`, `MKCOL`, `COPY`, `MOVE`, `REPORT` for WebDAV and CalDAV, in upper case.

## Switching orientation during a session (2.18)

`display.orientation` only decides the orientation at launch. When the user should be able to switch at any time (viewing pictures, reading long text, dashboards), call `ctx.screen:set_orientation(o)`.

```lua
function on_load(ctx)
  -- The last choice is kept in ctx.state, so the first frame already uses it
  if ctx.state.orientation then
    ctx.screen:set_orientation(ctx.state.orientation)
  end
end

local function toggle(ctx)
  local o = ctx.screen.orientation == "landscape" and "portrait" or "landscape"
  ctx.state.orientation = o
  ctx.screen:set_orientation(o)
end
```

- Values are `"portrait"`, `"landscape"` and `"default"` (back to the orientation this session opened with).
- It takes effect after the current callback returns: inside this callback the size in `ctx.screen` does not change, and the next callback gets the new `width`, `height` and `orientation`, with a full-refresh redraw scheduled by the host.
- It lasts only for this session and does not change the system setting; the orientation from before opening is restored when the session ends.
- Off-screen layers do not change size with rotation and their content is not guaranteed to survive, so redraw after rotating. Pointer coordinates follow the new orientation. In a lock-screen session it returns `nil, "inactive"`.

## Testing in the preview and on a device

| | Device | Studio preview |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ctx.system:open("file" / "book")` | Yes | Runs the same checks as the device (name, whether the file exists, extension, permission) but does not draw the reader; `open` only ends the session. Test reading progress and the return flow on a device |
| `ctx.device:keep_awake` | Yes | Callable; it only records the last value and there is no automatic power-off to observe |
| `save`, `timeout_ms` and the new methods of `ctx.net:request` | Yes | Yes |
| `ctx.screen:set_orientation` | Yes | Yes; the picture is redrawn in the new orientation |

In the preview `can_open` is false when the file is not in the folder; write a branch that shows another hint when it cannot open, and both sides work.

local function read_now(ctx, name)
  if not ctx.system:can_open("file", { name = name }) then
    ctx.dialog:toast("Cannot open this file")
    return
  end
  ctx.system:open("file", { name = name })   -- ends this session after the current callback returns
end

# 打开阅读器、系统页面和别的应用，保持唤醒、下载与切换方向

这一篇讲把用户带到别处、以及几件常用的设备能力：把书交给系统阅读器打开（2.20），列出卡上全部书、取书封（2.33），打开云同步、字体页和键盘词典（2.27），打开别的轻应用（2.32），休眠、关机与全刷（2.32），保持唤醒（2.18），把联网下载的内容直接存成文件（2.18），在会话中切换横竖屏（2.18）。完整规则见规范第 25、22、13、14、3 节。

## 把书交给阅读器（2.20）

书源、下载类应用把 epub 或 txt 存进应用文件夹以后，不用自己做阅读界面：`ctx.system:open("file", ...)` 直接交给系统阅读器。阅读进度、最近阅读和阅读统计都和用户自己从文件管理里打开一样，用户从阅读器返回时回到本应用（一次新的会话）。

![书架按 can_open 决定按钮；菜谱看板保持唤醒，并在会话中切到横屏](/docs/reader/open-rotate-zh.webp)

```lua
local function read_now(ctx, name)
  if not ctx.system:can_open("file", { name = name }) then
    ctx.dialog:toast("打不开这个文件")
    return
  end
  ctx.system:open("file", { name = name })   -- 当前回调返回后结束本次会话
end
```

- **文件**：`name` 是 `AppFiles/<app_id>/` 这一层里的文件名，不能写路径。2.20 能打开 `epub`、`txt`、`xtc`、`xtch`、`xtcz`，`.xtapp` 和没有扩展名的文件不行。
- **书**：`ctx.system:open("book", { id = book.id })` 打开 `ctx.reader:books()` 或 `current()` 给出的书，需要权限 `reader`；只出现在 `all_books()` 里的书不认。2.33 的包还认 `library()` 给出的书，见下一节。
- `open` 在当前回调返回后才生效，会调用 `on_leave`，所以打开之前先把状态存进 `ctx.state`。不能指定章节或页码。
- 先用 `can_open(target, opts)` 判断：文件不存在、扩展名没有阅读器、没有存储卡、锁屏会话时它都是 false；`open` 对应返回 `nil, "not_found"`、`nil, "not_supported"` 或 `nil, "invalid_argument"`。
- 不带 `opts` 时 `can_open("file")` 回答的是「这台设备支持这个目标吗」，旧设备上是 false，据此降级，不要看 `ctx.api.minor`。

## 列出卡上全部书与取书封（2.33）

`books()` 只给最近读的 18 本。书架、书城类应用要列出存储卡上的全部书（包括从没打开过的书）时，用 `ctx.reader:library(opts)`，它分页给出系统书架「全部」里的书。需要权限 `reader`，manifest 的 `api` 至少写 `"2.33"`；更早的包上 `ctx.reader.library` 为 nil。

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.33", "permissions": ["reader"]
local PAGE = 20

local function load_page(ctx, page)
  local r, err = ctx.reader:library({ offset = page * PAGE, limit = PAGE, sort = "title" })
  if not r then
    if err == "busy" then   -- 插卡后系统书架还在「正在整理」，过一会儿再取
      ctx:after(3000, function(ctx) load_page(ctx, page) end)
    end
    status = err
    return
  end
  total, books = r.total, r.books
  ctx:invalidate()
end

-- 用户选了一本：没打开过的书也能直接交给阅读器
ctx.system:open("book", { id = books[i].id })
```

- **参数**（都可省略）：`offset` 从 0 起；`limit` 1–50，默认 20；`sort` 为 `"recent"`（默认，读过的在前）、`"added"`、`"title"`、`"author"`、`"size"`；`status` 为 `"all"`、`"unread"`、`"reading"`、`"finished"`；`format` 为 `"all"`、`"epub"`、`"txt"`、`"xtc"`（含 `xtch`、`xtcz`）。
- **返回** `{ total, books }`：`total` 是符合筛选的总数，不随分页变；`offset` 不小于 `total` 时 `books` 为空表。每本有 `id`、`title`、`author`、`format`、`status`、`percent`、`size`、`added`（可能为 nil）、`file`、`has_cover`。
- 数据来自系统书架的索引，不在调用时扫卡。用户刚拷进的书要等索引更新后才出现。
- **错误**：插卡后第一次建索引期间 `nil, "busy"`，稍后重试；没有存储卡 `nil, "not_found"`；参数取值不对 `nil, "invalid_argument"`；内存不足 `nil, "out_of_memory"`。
- `library()` 只读：不生成封面，也不改系统书架的排序和筛选。
- 2.33 的包用 `library()` 的 `id` 调 `ctx.system:open("book", ...)` 也认；书文件已删除时返回 `nil, "not_found"`。

**书封。** `cover(id)` 只取系统已经生成的封面，从没在书架上显示过的书拿不到。2.33 起可以写 `source = "epub"`，直接从 EPUB 文件里取封面图：

```lua
local img, err = ctx.reader:cover(book.id, { source = "epub", max_w = 160, max_h = 240 })
if img then covers[book.id] = img end   -- 取到就留着，不要每帧取
```

- 只对 EPUB 有效：别的格式返回 `nil, "not_supported"`；书里没有封面图片返回 `nil, "not_found"`。`has_cover` 为 true 也不保证一定取得到。
- `max_w`、`max_h` 等比缩小，默认屏幕尺寸；`gray` 与 `ctx.image:decode` 相同。图片格式不支持、损坏或太大时返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`。
- 每次都要打开书文件，较慢。一屏要很多封面时分几帧取。
- 封面是运行时图像：一个会话同时最多 8 张、合计 524288 字节，满了返回 `nil, "limit_exceeded"`。翻页时对不再显示的封面调用 `img:release()`。
- 结果不写进系统封面缓存。2.0–2.32 的包写了 `opts` 会被忽略，等同 `cover(id)`。

## 打开云同步、字体页和键盘词典（2.27）

应用缺东西时，可以把用户直接带到对应的系统页面：还没收到推送就去云同步，要换字体就去字体页，组合输入缺词典就去下载。用户从那一页返回时，回到本应用（一次新的会话）。

```lua
-- 用户点了「前往云同步」
local function go_sync(ctx)
  if ctx.system:can_open("cloud.sync") then
    ctx.state.page = "inbox"          -- open 会结束会话，先存好要回到的页面
    ctx.system:open("cloud.sync")
  end
end
```

| 目标 | 打开的页面 |
| --- | --- |
| `"cloud.sync"` | 云同步：已绑定显示同步列表，未绑定显示绑定页 |
| `"settings.font"` | 工具箱设置里的字体页，用户在这里选轻应用用的 TTF |
| `"settings.keyboard_dict"` | 系统设置「通用 → 键盘 → 下载词典」，组合输入要用的词典 |

- 不需要权限，manifest 不用改，2.0–2.26 的包也能用。用 `can_open(目标)` 判断宿主支持不支持，不要看 `ctx.api.minor`：正常会话里为 true，锁屏会话或设备没有这一页时为 false。
- `opts` 被忽略，不能指定页面里的内容。不支持或锁屏会话中 `open` 返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`。
- 只在用户明确点按之后调用。推送成功、下载完成时不要自动跳走，会打断用户正在做的事。
- 在云同步列表里打开已下载的书或应用时，按该页原有规则打开那一项，不回到本应用。

## 打开别的轻应用（2.32）

桌面、启动器、文件夹类应用可以用 `ctx.system:open("app", ...)` 打开另一个已安装的轻应用。它结束时回到本应用（一次新的会话）。需要权限 `apps`，`api` 至少写 `"2.32"`；`id` 从 `ctx.apps:list()` 或 `recent()` 取，见「已装应用：做桌面和启动器」。

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.32", "permissions": ["apps"]
local function launch(ctx, id)
  if not ctx.system:can_open("app", { id = id }) then
    ctx.dialog:toast("这个应用打不开")
    return
  end
  ctx.system:open("app", { id = id, open = { page = "today" } })
end
```

- **会话**：当前回调返回后结束本次会话（调用 `on_leave`），再打开目标应用。
- **回到本应用**：目标调用 `ctx:quit()`、返回键未处理、长按返回键强制退出、出错结束，都回到本应用。用户按系统键回主页、锁屏、关机时不回来。只记一层来源：目标再打开第三个应用，第三个结束后回到目标应用。
- **目标拿到什么**：目标这次的 `ctx.launch` 是 `{ source = "app", from = "<本应用的 app_id>", open = ... }`。`open` 原样转交，编码后不超过 191 字节；没写时没有这个字段。
- **错误**：没有 `apps` 权限、锁屏会话、`id` 缺失或为空、`id` 是本应用、`open` 不是表或太长，返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`；没装返回 `nil, "not_found"`；目标是 `outdated` 或本设备不满足它的 `requires`，返回 `nil, "not_supported"`。`can_open` 在这些情况下都为 false。
- 不带 `opts` 的 `can_open("app")` 在有 `apps` 权限的正常会话中为 true，用它判断宿主是否实现了 2.32。

## 休眠、关机与全刷（2.32）

`ctx.system:act(name)` 让系统做一件用户本来就能用实体键或系统菜单做的事。不需要权限，2.0–2.31 的包也能用。

```lua
function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.phase == "up" and hit(sleep_btn, ev) then
    local ok, err = ctx.system:act("sleep")   -- 只能在用户操作里调用
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

| `name` | 动作 |
| --- | --- |
| `"sleep"` | 进入锁屏，与短按电源键相同：结束本次会话（调用 `on_leave`），设备休眠 |
| `"power_off"` | 关机。系统先弹确认框（应用收到 `on_pause`、`on_resume`）；用户取消就回到本应用 |
| `"refresh"` | 下一帧全刷一次，与 `ctx:invalidate("full")` 相同 |

- `"sleep"`、`"power_off"` 只能在投递按键 `up` 或指针 `up` 的 `on_input` 里调用（包括它直接调用的函数）。在定时、`on_load`、`on_tick`、网络完成等回调里返回 `nil, "inactive"`：休眠和关机由用户决定。`"refresh"` 没有这条限制。
- 其他错误：不认识的 `name` 返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`；锁屏会话返回 `nil, "inactive"`；关机确认框正在显示时返回 `nil, "busy"`；`name` 不是字符串时抛出 Lua 错误。
- `"sleep"` 前先把状态存进 `ctx.state`，和 `open` 一样会结束会话。
- 刷新一般交给系统，不要定时调 `"refresh"`；只在用户点了「刷新屏幕」这类按钮时用。
- 前光用 `ctx.frontlight`，方向用上面的 `ctx.screen:set_orientation`，`act` 不重复这些。

## 计时和看板：保持唤醒（2.18）

番茄钟、菜谱步骤、看板这类「在用但没碰屏幕」的应用，放几分钟就会被系统自动关机打断。`ctx.device:keep_awake(ms)` 让系统在 `ms` 毫秒内不因空闲而关机。

```lua
local function on_tick(ctx)
  -- 每次续 10 分钟：应用在跑就一直有效，退出后自然失效
  ctx.device:keep_awake(10 * 60 * 1000)
end
```

- `ms` 是 0 到 14400000（4 小时）的整数，0 表示取消。再次调用从调用时刻重新计时，不累加；需要更久就在快到期时再调用一次。
- 只推迟、不提前：给得比系统剩余的空闲时间短，不会让设备更早关机。
- 只阻止空闲自动关机。按电源键仍然锁屏或关机；电量低于 5% 且没在充电时不阻止。
- 只在本会话内有效：退出、回主页、进入锁屏、出错都会立即失效。锁屏会话里返回 `nil, "inactive"`。
- 设备一直亮着更耗电，持续续期的应用要在说明里写明。Studio 预览没有自动关机，只记下最近一次的值。

## 下载大文件：保存到文件（2.18）

下载一本小说或一份大 JSON 时，不要把整个响应放进 `res.body`。给 `ctx.net:request` 设置 `save`，宿主把正文直接写进应用文件夹，再分段读。

```lua
ctx.net:request({
  url = "https://example.com/books/three-body.txt",
  save = { to = "files", name = "three-body.txt" },
  timeout_ms = 60000,
}, function(ctx, res)
  if res.saved then
    -- 下载完成，可以直接交给阅读器
    ctx.system:open("file", { name = "three-body.txt" })
  end
end)
```

- `timeout_ms` 是 1000–60000 的整数，默认 30000，是从调用起到收完响应的整个期限；2.17 及更早的设备忽略它，期限固定为 30000 毫秒。
- `res.saved` 为 true 表示文件已替换；没设置 `save` 时它是 nil。
- 2.18 起 `method` 还可以是 `PUT`、`PATCH`、`DELETE`、`HEAD`、`OPTIONS`，以及 WebDAV、CalDAV 用的 `PROPFIND`、`PROPPATCH`、`MKCOL`、`COPY`、`MOVE`、`REPORT`，必须大写。

## 会话中切换横竖屏（2.18）

`display.orientation` 只决定打开时的方向。需要让用户在应用里随时切换（看图、读长文、看板）时，调用 `ctx.screen:set_orientation(o)`。

```lua
function on_load(ctx)
  -- 上次的选择存在 ctx.state 里，打开时第一帧就按它画
  if ctx.state.orientation then
    ctx.screen:set_orientation(ctx.state.orientation)
  end
end

local function toggle(ctx)
  local o = ctx.screen.orientation == "landscape" and "portrait" or "landscape"
  ctx.state.orientation = o
  ctx.screen:set_orientation(o)
end
```

- 取值 `"portrait"`、`"landscape"`、`"default"`（回到本会话打开时的方向）。
- 当前回调返回后才生效：本次回调里 `ctx.screen` 的宽高不变，下一次回调才拿到新的 `width`、`height`、`orientation`，并且宿主会安排一次全刷重绘。
- 只在本会话有效，不改系统设置；会话结束后恢复打开前的方向。
- 离屏图层不随旋转改尺寸，内容也不保证保留，旋转后重新绘制；指针坐标按新方向换算。锁屏会话里返回 `nil, "inactive"`。

## 在预览和真机上测试

| | 真机 | Studio 预览 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ctx.system:open("file" / "book")` | 有 | 做与真机相同的检查（名字、文件是否存在、扩展名、权限），但不画阅读器，`open` 只结束会话；阅读进度和返回流程要在真机上试 |
| `ctx.device:keep_awake` | 有 | 能调用，只记下最近一次的值，没有自动关机可看 |
| `ctx.net:request` 的 `save`、`timeout_ms`、新方法 | 有 | 有 |
| `ctx.screen:set_orientation` | 有 | 有，画面按新方向重画 |

预览里文件夹里没有对应文件时 `can_open` 为 false，写成「不能打开就换一种提示」的分支，两边都能走通。

local function read_now(ctx, name)
  if not ctx.system:can_open("file", { name = name }) then
    ctx.dialog:toast("打不开这个文件")
    return
  end
  ctx.system:open("file", { name = name })   -- 当前回调返回后结束本次会话
end

# Saving and loading

This guide explains how to keep data that must survive after the app closes, and how to read it back. Four rules: keep small progress in `ctx.state` and data that keeps growing in private files; when loading, only fill in defaults and migrate by version number, and never replace the table; call `ctx:save_state()` after key actions and check its result; if `ctx.state` exceeds 16 KB, none of it is saved, and no error is reported.

## Where to keep it: ctx.state, private files or app files

| Data | Where | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current progress, settings, scores, current page, a small board | `ctx.state` (section 28) | The host saves it when the session ends and loads it on the next launch; you write no save code |
| Data that keeps growing: history, replays, maps, logs, offline caches | `ctx.storage` private files (section 9) | 256 KB per file, up to 512 files; `ctx.state` holds only 16 KB |
| Binary data, multiple save slots | `ctx.storage`, one file per slot | There is only one `ctx.state`, and its strings cannot contain 0 bytes |
| Files the user should see, copy out, or put in | `ctx.files` app files (section 29) | Stored in `AppFiles/<app_id>/` on the SD card and kept when the app is uninstalled; epub, txt and xtc files there can be handed to the reader with `ctx.system:open("file", { name = name })` (2.20) |

Use `ctx.state` by default, and move only the part that grows into files. You can use both together: `ctx.state` records the current position, and files hold the large data. Apps that rely on the auto-save must put `"api": "2.2"` or newer in the manifest: devices at 2.1 and below have no `ctx.state`.

Do not store values that can be computed from other values, such as production rates or remaining time; compute them each time. For a countdown, store the end time, not the time remaining (see "Clock faces and countdowns").

## Loading: fill in defaults, migrate by version

When a session starts, `ctx.state` is already loaded before the top-level code and `on_load` run. If there is no save, or the save is damaged, it is an empty table. Loading does only two things: it fills in missing fields with defaults, and it converts old formats to the new one.

Put loading, migration, and saving in one module that both the main program and the lock screen use:

```lua
-- save.lua
local M = {}
local FORMAT = 2                         -- save format this version understands

local function defaults(s)
  s.level = s.level or 1
  s.gold = (s.gold or 0) + 0.0           -- numbers that grow: back to float after loading
  s.settings = s.settings or {}
  if s.settings.sound == nil then s.settings.sound = true end
end

-- call once in on_load; returns the table to use this session
function M.load(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.v = s.v or 1
  if s.v > FORMAT then                   -- user reinstalled an older version; a newer one wrote this save
    local fresh = { v = FORMAT }         -- play with defaults, leave ctx.state alone
    defaults(fresh)
    return fresh
  end
  if s.v < 2 then                        -- format 1 called it coins, format 2 renamed it gold
    s.gold = s.coins
    s.coins = nil
    s.v = 2
  end
  defaults(s)
  return s
end

M.error = nil                            -- when not nil, show "save failed" in a corner of the screen

function M.save(ctx)
  local ok, err = ctx:save_state()
  M.error = not ok and err or nil
  return ok
end

return M
```

```lua
-- index.lua
local save = require("save")
local S

function on_load(ctx)
  S = save.load(ctx)
end
```

- Write defaults as `s.x = s.x or default`. Writing `ctx.state = { level = 1 }` in `on_load` replaces the save that was just loaded, and an empty save is written when the session ends.
- Boolean defaults need an `== nil` check: `s.sound = s.sound or true` turns a saved false back into true.
- Keep a format version `v` in the save, and increment it whenever you rename a field or change the structure (contract appendix B). When renaming a field, also read the old name, and keep that compatibility code for at least one version.
- When the save has a newer version than your app, do not modify `ctx.state`. The host writes to the card only when the content changes, so an unmodified table keeps the newer save intact. In that case, the code above provides a separate local table: the game remains playable, but progress from this session is not saved.

## When to save: automatic, plus manual saves at key moments

Every session end saves automatically: quitting, a forced exit by holding back, going to the home screen, opening a system page, entering the lock screen, and powering off. The following two cases do not save, and everything since the last save is lost:

- the script stops with an error before `on_leave`;
- sudden power loss, or a drained battery.

Therefore, call `ctx:save_state()` after actions that must not be lost, for example:

- after a round ends, a level is cleared, or a reward is collected;
- after buying, upgrading, or prestiging;
- after changing settings or finishing an edit.

Do not call it every frame in `on_tick` or `on_draw`. The time spent writing to the card counts against the current callback; writing 4 KB takes about 120 ms on X4 Pro. The host skips the write when nothing has changed, but each call still encodes the whole table.

When `ctx:save_state()` fails, the previous save is kept, and the call returns `nil, error`:

| Error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `limit_exceeded` | The save exceeds 16 KB as JSON; see the next section |
| `io_error` | There is no SD card, or it could not be written |
| `out_of_memory` | There is not enough memory to encode the save |
| `invalid_argument` | `ctx.state` was replaced with a value that is not a table |

At a minimum, show the failure, for example "save failed" in a corner of the screen. Otherwise, neither the user nor the author knows that progress is not being saved.

## ctx.state over 16 KB is not saved at all

`ctx.state` encoded as JSON must not exceed 16384 bytes. Over the limit, it is not truncated: the whole save is skipped, and the host keeps the previous one. When the automatic save at session end fails, nothing reports it; only the result of `ctx:save_state()` reveals it. As a result, from some point on, progress stays stuck at that old save.

- Leave headroom: keep the save under 8 KB in normal play. A Chinese character takes 3 bytes, so 16 KB is about five thousand characters.
- Look for fields that grow with play time: history, records, logs, chat, explored map cells, favorites. Either cap them and keep only the most recent entries, or move them into private files (see the next section).
- Do not copy data files from the package or whole network responses into `ctx.state`; store only indexes, ids, or progress.
- In the Studio preview, the run log shows a hint when the save exceeds 12 KB or was skipped because it exceeded the limit.

## What comes back different

| Saved | Loaded | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Floats with no fractional part, such as `2.0` and `100.0` | Integers `2`, `100` | For numbers that grow, write `s.x = s.x + 0.0` after loading; otherwise, values past `2147483647` wrap around to negative |
| String key `"12"` | Integer key `12` | Do not make string keys look like integers; for example, write `"id12"` |
| Float, boolean, or table keys | Missing | Use string keys |
| Functions, images, layers, and other objects | Missing | Store only the data needed to rebuild them, such as the image name |
| Tables at level 7 or deeper | Missing | Flatten the structure to at most 6 levels |
| Strings containing 0 bytes | Truncated at the 0 byte | Encode them with `ctx.base64:encode` before saving, or use a file |
| Local and global variables | Lost | Put everything that must be kept into `ctx.state` |

## Large data goes in private files

Put data that keeps growing into `ctx.storage` files, and keep only a small index in `ctx.state`:

```lua
local HISTORY = "history.json"
local MAX_RECORDS = 200                  -- cap the count so the file cannot grow forever
local history                            -- read on first use, then kept in memory

local function load_history(ctx)
  if history then return history end
  local raw = ctx.storage:read(HISTORY)  -- nil, "not_found" when the file does not exist
  local data = raw and ctx.json:decode(raw)
  history = type(data) == "table" and data or {}
  return history
end

-- call when a round ends
local function add_record(ctx, record)
  local list = load_history(ctx)
  list[#list + 1] = record
  if #list > MAX_RECORDS then table.remove(list, 1) end
  local text = ctx.json:encode(list)
  local ok, err = text and ctx.storage:write(HISTORY, text)
  if not ok then save.error = err end
  S.games = (S.games or 0) + 1           -- ctx.state keeps only the number of rounds
  save.save(ctx)
end
```

- Combine the data into a few files, and write them at key moments. Writing one 4 KB file takes about 120 ms on X4 Pro, so writing ten in one callback exceeds the time limit. Do not write every frame.
- `write` replaces the whole file. After a power loss during a write, you read either all of the old content or all of the new content, never half of it.
- JSON follows different rules from `ctx.state`: `ctx.json` object keys are always read back as strings; tables whose integer keys are not consecutive fail to encode (`invalid_argument`); `null` is read back as `ctx.json.null`, not nil.
- Keep a format version `v` in each file as well, and migrate it separately from `ctx.state`.
- Multiple save slots are multiple files, such as `slot1.json` and `slot2.json`; `ctx.state` records which one is in use.

When several kinds of data grow (backpack, logs, events, map), split them by kind into separate files, write only the files that changed, and switch the files together; see "When saves get large".

## Sharing files with other apps and the user: public folders (2.31)

The app's own `ctx.files` folder (`/AppFiles/<app_id>/`) is visible only to your app and the user. To exchange files with other apps, or to read books and images pushed by cloud sync, use the public folders. This needs the `folders` permission, which only packages with `api` 2.31 or later may declare; without it `ctx.files.folder` is nil.

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.31", "permissions": ["folders"]
local pub = ctx.files:folder("Public")
pub:mkdir("words/cet4")
local ok, err = pub:write("words/cet4/list.txt", text)
for _, e in ipairs(pub:list("words") or {}) do
  ctx.log:info(e.name .. (e.dir and "/" or ""))
end
local head = ctx.files:folder("Pushed Books"):read("dune.epub", 0, 4096)
```

| Folder | Use | Subfolders |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Public` | Exchanging files between apps, and between apps and the user | Yes |
| `Documents` `Downloads` `Pictures` `Music` | Documents, downloads, pictures, audio | Yes |
| `Pushed Books` `Pushed Images` `Pushed Fonts` | Books, images and fonts pushed by cloud sync | One level only |
| `Fonts` | Fonts the user put there | One level only |

- Names are case-sensitive and must be one of the nine above; anything else returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. `folder.path` is `"/" .. name`, for telling the user where to look. A folder that does not exist still returns an object and is created on the first write.
- Calls take paths: segments separated by `/`, at most 8 segments and 255 bytes in total, each segment following the app folder's name rules, no leading or trailing `/`. One-level folders accept a single segment; calling `mkdir` or `rmdir` on them, or passing a subfolder to `list`, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.
- Methods: `list(dir)` (items `{ name, size, dir }`; more than 512 items gives `nil, "limit_exceeded"`), `exists`, `size`, `read`, `write`, `append`, `remove`, `mkdir`, `rmdir`. Per-call limits and error codes for `read`, `write` and `append` are the same as `ctx.files`; `write` and `append` create missing parent subfolders.
- Common errors: a missing subfolder gives `nil, "not_found"`; `remove` on a subfolder, `rmdir` on a non-empty folder, or `mkdir` where a file has the same name gives `nil, "io_error"`.
- There is no 512-file quota and no total size limit. Reading and writing count against the callback limit, so read large files across several `ctx:after` calls.
- Uninstalling or upgrading does not delete these files. The system and the user read and write them too, so every call reflects what is on the card at that moment.

**Ask the user before deleting or overwriting.** Files in public folders may belong to the user or to other apps, and once deleted they are gone:

```lua
local function delete_shared(ctx, path)
  if not ctx.dialog then return end
  ctx.dialog:confirm({ title = "Delete file", message = "This deletes /Public/" .. path .. " for every app.", ok_text = "Delete" },
    function(ctx, ok)
      if ok then ctx.files:folder("Public"):remove(path) end
    end)
end
```

Files meant only for your app and the user still go in your own `ctx.files` folder, and the app's own data still goes in `ctx.storage`.

## The lock screen reads the same save

Each lock screen refresh (section 15) is a separate short session. It loads the `ctx.state` that the main program saved, but lock screen sessions do not save automatically.

![The main program and the lock screen read the same ctx.state](/docs/save/shared-en.webp)

- Compute the numbers the lock screen shows with the same module as the main program, and do not write them back to `ctx.state`.
- When the lock screen must change the save, call `ctx:save_state()` yourself.
- After the main program changes data that the lock screen uses, call `ctx:save_state()` immediately instead of waiting until exit.

end

# 存档与读档

说明应用关闭后仍需保留的数据如何保存和读回。要点有四条：较小的进度放在 `ctx.state` 中，会持续增长的数据放在私有文件中；读档时只补齐默认值、按版本号迁移，不整体替换；关键操作之后调用 `ctx:save_state()` 并检查返回值；`ctx.state` 超过 16 KB 时整份存档都不会保存，而且不会报错。

## 存在哪：ctx.state、私有文件还是应用文件

| 数据 | 存放位置 | 原因 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 当前进度、设置、分数、当前页、小棋盘 | `ctx.state`（契约第 28 节） | 宿主在会话结束时自动保存，下次打开时载入，无需编写存档代码 |
| 会持续增加的数据：历史记录、对局回放、地图、日志、离线缓存 | `ctx.storage` 私有文件（第 9 节） | 单个文件 256 KB，最多 512 个；`ctx.state` 只有 16 KB |
| 二进制数据、需要多个存档位 | `ctx.storage`，每个存档位一个文件 | `ctx.state` 只有一份，其中的字符串不能包含 0 字节 |
| 需要让用户查看、拷出或放入的文件 | `ctx.files` 应用文件（第 29 节） | 位于存储卡的 `AppFiles/<app_id>/` 中，卸载应用时也不会删除；其中的 epub、txt、xtc 可以用 `ctx.system:open("file", { name = name })`（2.20）交给阅读器打开 |

默认使用 `ctx.state`，只把会增长的部分移到文件中。两种方式可以同时使用：`ctx.state` 记录当前位置，文件存放大块数据。依赖自动存档的应用应在 manifest 中写入 `"api": "2.2"` 或更高版本：2.1 及以下版本的设备上没有 `ctx.state`。

可以由其他值计算得出的数据不保存，每次使用时重新计算，例如产出速度、剩余时间。倒计时保存结束时刻，而不是剩余时长（见「钟面与倒计时」）。

## 读档：补默认值，按版本号迁移

会话开始时，`ctx.state` 在顶层代码和 `on_load` 运行之前就已载入。没有存档或存档损坏时，它是一张空表。读档只做两件事：为缺失的字段补齐默认值，把旧格式转换为新格式。

将读档、迁移和存档放在一个模块中，供主程序和锁屏共同使用：

```lua
-- save.lua
local M = {}
local FORMAT = 2                         -- 这一版认识的存档格式

local function defaults(s)
  s.level = s.level or 1
  s.gold = (s.gold or 0) + 0.0           -- 会变大的数装回后换回浮点
  s.settings = s.settings or {}
  if s.settings.sound == nil then s.settings.sound = true end
end

-- on_load 里调用一次，返回这次会话要用的表
function M.load(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.v = s.v or 1
  if s.v > FORMAT then                   -- 用户装回了旧版本，存档是新版本写的
    local fresh = { v = FORMAT }         -- 按默认值玩，不碰 ctx.state
    defaults(fresh)
    return fresh
  end
  if s.v < 2 then                        -- 1 版叫 coins，2 版改名 gold
    s.gold = s.coins
    s.coins = nil
    s.v = 2
  end
  defaults(s)
  return s
end

M.error = nil                            -- 非 nil 时在画面角落提示「存档失败」

function M.save(ctx)
  local ok, err = ctx:save_state()
  M.error = not ok and err or nil
  return ok
end

return M
```

```lua
-- index.lua
local save = require("save")
local S

function on_load(ctx)
  S = save.load(ctx)
end
```

- 默认值写成 `s.x = s.x or 默认值`。如果在 `on_load` 中写 `ctx.state = { level = 1 }`，会替换刚载入的存档，会话结束时再保存为空的存档。
- 布尔值的默认值需要判断 `== nil`：`s.sound = s.sound or true` 会把保存的 false 改回 true。
- 在存档中放一个格式版本号 `v`，每次修改字段名或结构时加一（契约附录 B）。字段改名时同时读取旧名称，兼容代码至少保留一个版本。
- 读到比当前应用更新的版本时，不要修改 `ctx.state`。宿主只在内容变化时写入存储卡，表未被修改，新版本的存档就能完整保留。上面的写法在这种情况下另外提供一张局部表，游戏仍可正常进行，只是本次进度不会保存。

## 什么时候存：自动存，加上关键时刻手动存

会话结束时都会自动保存，包括：退出、长按返回强制退出、回到主页、打开系统页面、进入锁屏、关机。以下两种情况不会自动保存，上次存档之后的所有操作都会丢失：

- 脚本在 `on_leave` 之前因出错而结束；
- 突然断电，或电池耗尽。

因此，在不能丢失的操作之后调用 `ctx:save_state()`，例如：

- 一局结束、过关、获得奖励之后；
- 购买、升级、转生之后；
- 修改设置、完成一条内容的编辑之后。

不要在 `on_tick`、`on_draw` 中每帧调用。写入存储卡的耗时计入当前回调，在 X4 Pro 上写入 4 KB 约需 120 ms。内容未变化时宿主不写入存储卡，但每次调用仍会对整张表进行一次编码。

`ctx:save_state()` 失败时，原存档保持不变，返回 `nil, 错误名`：

| 错误 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `limit_exceeded` | 存档编码为 JSON 后超过 16 KB，见下一节 |
| `io_error` | 没有存储卡，或无法写入 |
| `out_of_memory` | 内存不足，无法编码 |
| `invalid_argument` | `ctx.state` 被替换为非表的值 |

至少应把失败显示出来，例如在画面角落显示「存档失败」，否则用户和作者都无法得知进度没有保存。

## ctx.state 超过 16 KB 会整份不存

`ctx.state` 编码为 JSON 后不能超过 16384 字节。超出时不会截断，而是整份存档都不保存，宿主保留上一份存档。会话结束时的自动存档失败不会有任何提示，只能通过 `ctx:save_state()` 的返回值发现。其结果是：从某一时刻起，进度会一直停留在那份旧存档上。

- 留出余量，正常游戏时将存档控制在 8 KB 以内。一个中文字符占 3 字节，16 KB 约相当于五千个汉字。
- 检查哪些字段会随游戏时间增长：历史、记录、日志、聊天、已探索的地图格子、收藏列表。对这些字段，要么设置条数上限、只保留最近的记录，要么移到私有文件中（见下一节）。
- 不要把包内的数据文件或网络返回的完整内容复制到 `ctx.state` 中，只保存下标、id 或进度。
- 在 Studio 预览中，存档超过 12 KB，或因超出上限而未保存时，运行日志会给出提示。

## 存进去和读回来不一样的地方

| 保存的值 | 读回的值 | 处理方法 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2.0`、`100.0` 这类没有小数部分的浮点数 | 整数 `2`、`100` | 对会持续增长的数值，载入后执行 `s.x = s.x + 0.0`，否则超过 `2147483647` 时会环绕为负数 |
| 字符串键 `"12"` | 整数键 `12` | 不要把字符串键写成整数的形式，例如改写为 `"id12"` |
| 以小数、布尔值或表作键 | 该项缺失 | 改用字符串键 |
| 函数、图像、图层等对象 | 该项缺失 | 只保存能重新创建这些对象的数据，例如图片名 |
| 第 7 层及更深层的表 | 该项缺失 | 将结构扁平化，最多 6 层 |
| 包含 0 字节的字符串 | 在 0 字节处截断 | 先用 `ctx.base64:encode` 编码再保存，或改存到文件中 |
| 局部变量、全局变量 | 不再存在 | 需要保留的数据都放在 `ctx.state` 中 |

## 大块数据放私有文件

会持续增加的数据放在 `ctx.storage` 的文件中，`ctx.state` 只记录较小的索引：

```lua
local HISTORY = "history.json"
local MAX_RECORDS = 200                  -- 条数设上限，文件不会无限长
local history                            -- 第一次用时读，之后用内存里的

local function load_history(ctx)
  if history then return history end
  local raw = ctx.storage:read(HISTORY)  -- 没有这个文件时是 nil, "not_found"
  local data = raw and ctx.json:decode(raw)
  history = type(data) == "table" and data or {}
  return history
end

-- 一局结束时调用
local function add_record(ctx, record)
  local list = load_history(ctx)
  list[#list + 1] = record
  if #list > MAX_RECORDS then table.remove(list, 1) end
  local text = ctx.json:encode(list)
  local ok, err = text and ctx.storage:write(HISTORY, text)
  if not ok then save.error = err end
  S.games = (S.games or 0) + 1           -- ctx.state 里只记局数
  save.save(ctx)
end
```

- 将数据合并为少数几个文件，并在关键时刻写入。在 X4 Pro 上写入一个 4 KB 的文件约需 120 ms，一次回调中写入十个文件就会超时。不要每帧写入。
- `write` 会整体替换文件。写入过程中断电时，读到的要么是完整的旧内容，要么是完整的新内容，不会出现只写入一半的情况。
- JSON 的规则与 `ctx.state` 不同：`ctx.json` 的对象键读回后都是字符串；整数键不连续的表编码会失败（`invalid_argument`）；`null` 读回为 `ctx.json.null`，而不是 nil。
- 文件中同样放一个格式版本号 `v`，与 `ctx.state` 分开迁移。
- 多个存档位就是多个文件，例如 `slot1.json`、`slot2.json`，并在 `ctx.state` 中记录当前使用的是哪一个。

多种数据都会增长时（背包、日志、事件、地图），按种类拆分为多个文件，只写入修改过的文件，并同时切换多个文件，见「存档变大以后」。

## 和别的应用、用户共享文件：公共文件夹（2.31）

`ctx.files` 自己的文件夹（`/AppFiles/<app_id>/`）只有本应用和用户能看到。要和别的应用交换文件，或者要读云同步推送的书和图片，用公共文件夹。需要权限 `folders`，只允许 `api` 至少 2.31 的包声明；没声明时 `ctx.files.folder` 为 nil。

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.31", "permissions": ["folders"]
local pub = ctx.files:folder("Public")
pub:mkdir("词库/四级")
local ok, err = pub:write("词库/四级/list.txt", text)
for _, e in ipairs(pub:list("词库") or {}) do
  ctx.log:info(e.name .. (e.dir and "/" or ""))
end
local head = ctx.files:folder("Pushed Books"):read("三体.epub", 0, 4096)
```

| 文件夹 | 用途 | 子文件夹 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Public` | 应用之间、应用与用户之间交换文件 | 可以 |
| `Documents` `Downloads` `Pictures` `Music` | 文档、下载、图片、音频 | 可以 |
| `Pushed Books` `Pushed Images` `Pushed Fonts` | 云同步推送的书、图片、字体 | 只有一层 |
| `Fonts` | 用户自己放的字体 | 只有一层 |

- 名字区分大小写，只能是上表九个之一，其他返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`。`folder.path` 是 `"/" .. name`，用来告诉用户位置。文件夹不存在也照常返回对象，第一次写入时建好。
- 调用用路径：`/` 分开，最多 8 段，合计 ≤ 255 字节，每段按应用文件夹的名字规则，不以 `/` 开头或结尾。「只有一层」的文件夹只接受一段，对它调 `mkdir`、`rmdir` 或给 `list` 传子文件夹返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`。
- 方法：`list(dir)`（每项 `{ name, size, dir }`，超过 512 项 `nil, "limit_exceeded"`）、`exists`、`size`、`read`、`write`、`append`、`remove`、`mkdir`、`rmdir`。`read`、`write`、`append` 的单次上限和错误码与 `ctx.files` 相同；`write`、`append` 自动建好缺少的上级子文件夹。
- 常见错误：子文件夹不存在 `nil, "not_found"`；`remove` 的是子文件夹、`rmdir` 的文件夹不空、`mkdir` 遇到同名文件，返回 `nil, "io_error"`。
- 没有 512 个文件的额度，也不设总字节上限。读写耗时计入回调上限，大文件分几次 `ctx:after` 读。
- 卸载、升级都不删这些文件。系统和用户也在读写，每次都以卡上当时的内容为准。

**删除或覆盖前先问用户。** 公共文件夹里的文件可能是用户的、别的应用的，删了就没了：

```lua
local function delete_shared(ctx, path)
  if not ctx.dialog then return end
  ctx.dialog:confirm({ title = "删除文件", message = "将删除 /Public/" .. path .. "，别的应用也用不了了。", ok_text = "删除" },
    function(ctx, ok)
      if ok then ctx.files:folder("Public"):remove(path) end
    end)
end
```

只给本应用和用户的文件仍放 `ctx.files` 自己的文件夹，应用自己的数据仍放 `ctx.storage`。

## 锁屏读到的是同一份存档

锁屏脚本（第 15 节）每刷新一次就是一次独立的短会话。它载入的是主程序保存的 `ctx.state`，但锁屏会话不会自动保存。

![主程序和锁屏读的是同一份 ctx.state](/docs/save/shared-zh.webp)

- 锁屏上要显示的数值，用与主程序相同的模块计算，不写回 `ctx.state`。
- 确实需要在锁屏中修改存档时，自行调用 `ctx:save_state()`。
- 主程序修改了锁屏要用的数据后，立即调用 `ctx:save_state()`，不要等到退出时再保存。
entries.example:
-- save.lua
local M = {}
local FORMAT = 2                         -- 这一版认识的存档格式

local function defaults(s)
  s.level = s.level or 1
  s.gold = (s.gold or 0) + 0.0           -- 会变大的数装回后换回浮点
  s.settings = s.settings or {}
  if s.settings.sound == nil then s.settings.sound = true end
end

-- on_load 里调用一次，返回这次会话要用的表
function M.load(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.v = s.v or 1
  if s.v > FORMAT then                   -- 用户装回了旧版本，存档是新版本写的
    local fresh = { v = FORMAT }         -- 按默认值玩，不碰 ctx.state
    defaults(fresh)
    return fresh
  end
  if s.v < 2 then                        -- 1 版叫 coins，2 版改名 gold
    s.gold = s.coins
    s.coins = nil
    s.v = 2
  end
  defaults(s)
  return s
end

M.error = nil                            -- 非 nil 时在画面角落提示「存档失败」

function M.save(ctx)
  local ok, err = ctx:save_state()
  M.error = not ok and err or nil
  return ok
end

return M

# Building apps with an AI assistant and the local plugin

## What the plugin is

The XTApp plugin is a local service (MCP) on your computer. Once installed, AI assistants such as Codex, Cursor and WorkBuddy can read and write **the app folder on your computer**, send it to the Studio preview page to run, and press keys, tap and take screenshots for you.

It does not run Lua itself; the simulator is always the Studio preview page. It also never saves your project to the cloud. Install it from "Let AI control Studio" in the Studio top bar.

| AI tool | How | Difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | Marketplace plugin | Adds a preview status panel on the right |
| Cursor | MCP | Opens the preview page in Cursor's built-in browser |
| WorkBuddy and other tools | Generic MCP | No panel; the AI gives you the preview link to open |

## What a preview does

1. The plugin reads `manifest.json`, `*.lua`, text under `data/` and `lang/`, and images under `assets/` and `raw/` in the folder. It skips `docs/`, `tmp/` and `prototypes/`. Each text file can be up to 256KB, each image up to 2MB.
2. It sends them to Studio through a temporary relay that expires after 15 idle minutes: everything the first time, only changes after that.
3. The Studio preview page writes them into a project **in your browser** and runs it in the simulator.

The AI gives you the preview link, which carries a session id. Open it and keep it open. If a sign-in page appears, sign in yourself; the AI does not type your password. If two tabs open the same session, the last one opened takes over. Previewing the same folder again returns to the same project.

## Where your work lives

| Where | What | Can it be lost? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The app folder on your computer | The master copy of your source; this is what the AI edits | Like any file; use Git |
| The Studio project in your browser | The preview copy, plus images you uploaded or generated in Studio | Gone if you clear browser data or switch computers |
| Cloud workspace | The draft as of your last Save | No; sign in on any computer to open it |
| Simulator storage card `/AppFiles/<app_id>/` | Data your app saved with `ctx.files`, not source | Stays with the preview device |

- **Preview sync is not saving.** Each preview only updates the project in your browser. To open it on another computer, click Save in the top bar. If the cloud has a newer copy, Studio asks before overwriting; it never merges.
- **Saving is not publishing.** A saved draft is visible only to you. Store publishing is in the account dashboard.

## Which project a folder maps to

Studio looks in this order:

1. The folder has `docs/studio.cloud.json` containing `{"cloudProjectId": "…"}`: use that cloud project.
2. Last time it was this same folder: keep using it.
3. A project named like `display_name` in `manifest.json`, or **exactly one** draft with that name in your account.
4. Nothing matches: create a new project.

Except when creating, Studio asks "Allow the local plugin to sync into “…”?" before overwriting an existing project. Cancel if it is not the one you want.

To continue on another computer, bring the app folder with you. If your account has exactly one draft with that name, it is matched automatically. If there are several, a new project is created, and when you Save, Studio asks which draft to update and shows its cloud project id. To always match reliably, put that id in `docs/studio.cloud.json`. The file only matters on your computer; it does not go into the cloud draft or the store package. To start a separate copy, choose "Save as a new cloud project" in the project manager.

**Overwrite an existing project with the folder** (for example one you edited under another account, while the store listing is tied to this one): tell the AI "overwrite Studio project <cloud project id> with this folder". Studio asks you first; cancel and nothing changes. The confirm dialog spells out:

- **Will be replaced:** code, assets and settings come from the folder; files and images in Studio that the folder does not have are deleted.
- **Stays the same:** the project id, cloud project and store listing link; `app_id` (devices see the same app and players keep their saves); chat history; your store listing, since overwriting only changes your own project and the listing updates only after you save to the cloud and the review passes.
- **If something goes wrong:** a "Before overwrite" snapshot is saved first and can be restored from History; a failure partway restores the project automatically, never half replaced.

Afterwards the AI writes the id and `app_id` back into the folder so later syncs carry on normally.

## Files and images: which side wins

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| You changed or added files or images in the folder | Sent on the next preview |
| You deleted files or images the folder sent before | Deleted in Studio too |
| Images uploaded or generated in Studio | Kept on preview; the AI tells you once |
| Bring Studio images back into the folder | Ask the AI to pull them; images are saved as `assets/<name>.xic`, and differing local files are not overwritten by default |
| Delete an image that exists only in Studio | Tell the AI which one |

PNG, JPG and WebP are converted to XIC when sent.

Code you edit directly in Studio does not flow back to the folder; the next preview replaces it with the folder's version. Ask the AI to pull it first if you want to keep it.

## FAQ

| Symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The preview page shows sign-in | Sign in, then return to the same preview link |
| The AI says the preview is not connected | The preview page is not open; open the link again |
| "XTApp plugin needs an update" appears | Ask the AI to upgrade the XTApp plugin, then start a new conversation |
| It synced into the wrong project | Cancel the confirm dialog, or put the right id in `docs/studio.cloud.json` |
| The project is empty on another computer | You never clicked Save. Preview again from the folder, then Save |
| The AI cannot read or write the storage card | Needs `manifest.api` 2.9 or later, an `app_id`, and the preview showing this project |

entries.content:
# 用 AI 助手和本地插件做应用

## 插件是什么

XTApp 插件是装在你电脑上的一个本地服务（MCP）。装好以后，Codex、Cursor、WorkBuddy 等 AI 助手可以读写**你电脑上的应用文件夹**，把它推到 Studio 的预览页里跑，再替你按键、点屏、截图。

它不自己运行 Lua，模拟器始终是 Studio 预览页；它也不会把工程存到云上。安装入口在 Studio 顶栏「让 AI 操控 Studio」。

| AI 工具 | 接法 | 区别 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | 市场插件 | 多一个右侧预览状态面板 |
| Cursor | MCP | 用 Cursor 自带浏览器打开预览页 |
| WorkBuddy 等其他工具 | 通用 MCP | 没有面板，AI 把预览地址交给你打开 |

## 一次预览发生了什么

1. 插件读取文件夹里的 `manifest.json`、`*.lua`、`data/` 和 `lang/` 下的文本、`assets/` 和 `raw/` 下的图片。`docs/`、`tmp/`、`prototypes/` 不读。单个文本文件最大 256KB，单张图最大 2MB。
2. 内容经过一个临时中转发给 Studio，中转 15 分钟不用就过期。第一次全量，之后只发改动。
3. Studio 预览页把它写进**浏览器里**的一份工程，在模拟器里运行。

预览地址由 AI 给你，带一串会话号，请打开并保持开着。出现登录页就自己登录，AI 不替你填密码。同一个会话开了两个标签页时，最后打开的那个生效。同一个文件夹再次预览，会回到同一份工程。

## 东西存在哪

| 在哪 | 是什么 | 会不会丢 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 你电脑上的应用文件夹 | 源码的正本，AI 改的就是这里 | 和普通文件一样，建议用 Git |
| 浏览器里的 Studio 工程 | 预览用的副本，加上你在 Studio 里上传或生成的图 | 清浏览器数据、换电脑就没了 |
| 云工作区 | 你点「保存」时的那份草稿 | 不会，换电脑登录就能打开 |
| 模拟器存储卡 `/AppFiles/<app_id>/` | 应用用 `ctx.files` 存的数据，不是源码 | 跟着预览设备 |

- **预览同步不等于保存。** 每次预览只更新浏览器里的工程。要换电脑也能打开，在顶栏点「保存」。云上有更新的一份时，Studio 会问你要不要覆盖，不会自动合并。
- **保存不等于发布。** 保存后的草稿只有你自己看得见，上架商店在账号后台。

## 文件夹对应哪个工程

Studio 按这个顺序找：

1. 文件夹里有 `docs/studio.cloud.json`，写着 `{"cloudProjectId": "…"}`：用这份云工程。
2. 上次就是这个文件夹：接着用。
3. 和 `manifest.json` 里 `display_name` 同名的工程，或者账号里**只有一份**的同名草稿。
4. 都对不上：新建一份。

除了新建，覆盖已有工程前 Studio 都会问「允许本地插件同步到「…」？」，不是想要的那份就取消。

换一台电脑继续时，把应用文件夹带过去。账号里只有一份同名草稿会自动对上；有好几份时会新建，保存时 Studio 让你选更新哪一份，那里能看到云工程编号。想以后都稳稳对上，把编号写进 `docs/studio.cloud.json`。这个文件只在你电脑上起作用，不进云上的草稿，也不进商店包。想另开一份，在项目管理里选「另存为新的云工程」。

**用文件夹整份覆盖一个已有工程**（比如换账号改过、但商品绑在这里的那份）：告诉 AI「用这个文件夹覆盖 Studio 里的工程 <云工程编号>」。Studio 会先弹框问你，点取消就什么都不改。确认框会写清：

- **会换掉：** 代码、素材和配置换成文件夹里的；Studio 里有、文件夹里没有的文件和图片会删掉。
- **不会变：** 工程编号、云工程和已上架商品的关联；`app_id`（设备上还是同一个应用，玩家存档不受影响）；对话记录；已上架的商品——覆盖只改你自己的工程，保存到云、送审通过后商品才更新。
- **万一出问题：** 覆盖前自动存一份「覆盖前快照」，随时能在历史里退回；中途失败会自动退回原样，不会留下改了一半的项目。

覆盖完 AI 会把编号和 `app_id` 写回文件夹，以后照常同步。

## 文件和图片：哪边说了算

| 情况 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 文件夹里改了或加了文件、图片 | 下次预览推过去 |
| 文件夹里删了以前推过的文件、图片 | Studio 里也删掉 |
| 图片是在 Studio 里上传或生成的 | 预览时保留，AI 会告诉你一次 |
| 想把 Studio 里的图拿回文件夹 | 让 AI 拉回来，图片存成 `assets/<名字>.xic`；文件夹里已有且不同的默认不覆盖 |
| 想删掉只在 Studio 里的图 | 告诉 AI 删哪张 |

PNG、JPG、WebP 推过去时会转成 XIC。

你在 Studio 里直接改的代码不会自动回到文件夹，下次预览时文件夹里的版本会盖掉它。要留下，先让 AI 拉回来。

## 常见问题

| 现象 | 怎么办 |
| --- | --- |
| 预览页是登录页 | 自己登录，再回到同一个预览地址 |
| AI 说没连上预览 | 预览页没开或关掉了，重新打开 AI 给的地址 |
| 弹出「XTApp 插件需要更新」 | 对 AI 说「升级 XTApp 插件」，升级后新开一轮对话 |
| 同步到了别的工程 | 在确认框取消；或在 `docs/studio.cloud.json` 写上要用的编号 |
| 换电脑后工程是空的 | 之前没点过保存。文件夹还在就重新预览，再保存 |
| AI 读写存储卡失败 | 需要 `manifest.api` 2.9 以上、有 `app_id`，并且预览页正显示这个工程 |

# Studio JavaScript 文本文件工具

`run_javascript` 是 Studio Agent 用来一次性整理当前项目文本文件的工具。它在浏览器中执行 JavaScript；正式、稳定的项目操作能力只通过 `studio` 对象提供。它不能访问本机文件系统、终端、Python 或二进制素材。

## 何时使用

用户要求对 TXT、TSV 或 JSON 做规范化、键值转换、提取、筛选、去重、排序、正则替换、合并、拆分，或需要同时处理多个文本文件时，优先调用 `run_javascript`。保存在 `tmp/` 中的长文本同样适用：在脚本内读取和处理，不要通过 `read_file` 把全文送入对话上下文。

只创建或完整覆盖一个已知的小文本文件时，直接使用 `write_file`。

## 查看与读取

- `studio.listFiles()`：返回全部项目文本文件的 `{ path, size }` 列表；`size` 为字符数。
- `studio.findFiles(RegExp | string)`：按路径正则筛选文件；字符串按正则表达式处理，而不是 glob。
- `studio.exists(path)`：文件存在时返回 `true`；文件不存在或路径不受支持时返回 `false`。
- `studio.readFile(path)`：读取完整的 UTF-8 文本；文件不存在或路径不合法时抛出错误。
- `studio.readLines(path)`：按 `\n` 或 `\r\n` 拆分为字符串数组。
- `studio.readJson(path)`：读取文本并执行 `JSON.parse`；JSON 无效时抛出错误。

## 写入与格式化

- `studio.writeFile(path, text)`：新建或完整覆盖 UTF-8 文本文件。
- `studio.writeLines(path, lines)`：将字符串数组用换行符连接后写入。
- `studio.writeJson(path, value, spacing = 2)`：将 JSON 格式化后写入，默认使用两个空格缩进，并保留末尾换行。
- `studio.log(value)`：将调试信息写入本次工具结果；日志和返回值的长度均受限制。

写入的 `manifest.json` 必须是有效的 JSON。写入新的 `data/*.tsv` 或 `data/*.txt` 时，会自动在 `manifest.data_files` 中登记声明；覆盖已有的 data 文件时，仍必须遵守它已声明的 `max_bytes`，超出限制时由项目校验明确报告，不能静默绕过。

## 移动、复制与删除

- `studio.moveFile(from, to)`：实际移动文件，原路径不再存在；目标已存在时抛出错误，绝不覆盖。
- `studio.renameFile(from, to)`：`moveFile` 的别名。
- `studio.copyFile(from, to)`：创建独立的副本；目标不得已存在。
- `studio.deleteFile(path)`：删除文件。

移动、重命名、复制或删除 `data/*.tsv|txt` 时，`manifest.data_files` 随实际文件同步更新。`manifest.json`、当前主入口及启用中的锁屏入口是受保护文件，不能删除；移动入口脚本时，它必须保留在根目录，并保持 `.lua` 扩展名。

## 支持路径与边界

可操作的项目文本路径为：`manifest.json`、根目录的 Lua、`domain/*.lua`、`persistence/*.lua`、兼容的 `scripts/*.lua`、`data/*.tsv|txt`、`lang/*.tsv`、`docs/` 下的常见文本与源码（包括 `txt/md/markdown/mdx/csv/tsv/json/jsonc/yaml/yml/xml/html/css` 以及 `ts/tsx/js/jsx/vue/py/go/rs/sql` 等），以及 `tmp/*.txt` 与 `tmp/*.svg`。`docs/` 不是运行时代码目录，只用于保存资料和样例。

`assets/`、`raw/`、`dist/` 以及其他二进制目录或受管理目录不在文本工具的范围内。XIC 素材只能通过素材管线写入：脚本可以调用 `writeFile('tmp/icon.svg', svg)`，或调用 `studio.queueSvgAsset({ key, svg, width, height })` / `studio.queueGeneratedAsset({ key, emoji, width, height })`，由宿主按与上传相同的管线生成 XIC，透明范围与源图一致（见《素材与绘图》）。

## JavaScript 与提交方式

脚本可以使用普通 JavaScript 的 `RegExp`、`String.replace`、`String.matchAll`、`Map`、`Set`、数组方法、`JSON`、`Date`、`TextEncoder`、`TextDecoder` 与 `crypto.subtle`。

Studio 项目文件会先复制到脚本的工作副本中。脚本正常结束后，所有修改才一次性提交；出现未捕获的异常时，项目文件不会提交，因此不会留下未完成的修改。需要记录预期的失败时，在脚本中用 `try/catch` 捕获，再写入报告。

该脚本作为受信任的代码直接在浏览器环境中执行，没有强制超时；死循环可能使当前页面失去响应。浏览器的其他全局能力不是稳定、承诺支持的 Studio 项目 API，Agent 只应使用 `studio` 提供的项目操作能力。

## 示例：逐行转换键值文本

```js
const output = studio.readLines('tmp/input.txt')
  .map(line => line.replace(/:/g, '='))
studio.writeLines('docs/normalized.txt', output)
```

## 示例：批量移动临时文本

```js
for (const path of studio.findFiles(/^tmp\/.*\.txt$/)) {
  const name = path.slice('tmp/'.length)
  studio.moveFile(path, `docs/${name}`)
}
```

# Text and fonts

Start with the first section: for any font size, use `font_px(ctx, px)`. It is built on `ctx.fonts:size` and accepts any size from 8 to 96. The device user chooses the font in the system settings, and apps do not, so glyph widths vary from user to user: **always measure widths, centering, and wrapping; never hard-code them.** The code in the first section is only a few lines; copy it as is. To shrink a line that does not fit, see the second section. Later sections cover centering, paging, and the details of `ctx.fonts:size`.

## Fonts and sizes: what to use (start here)

**Rule: for any font size, use `font_px(ctx, px)`. It uses the font the user chose, at any size from 8 to 96; apps never choose a font or look up a font file. For text larger than 96, use an image; see the next section.**

Body text at 24 and titles at 30 are only the system presets. Games and visually rich apps should use a range of font sizes: large, prominent numbers, layered headings, and small notes in a corner, each at a suitable size. If the design uses 14, 18, 20, and 26, write `font_px(ctx, 14)` and so on; do not round them into a few ready-made steps.

![One line from 14 to 96 px, and a page that uses size for hierarchy (Studio preview)](/docs/text/sizes-en.webp)

Copy these lines into `main.lua`. After that, get a font by calling `font_px(ctx, px)`. When a size only draws specific characters, pass them as the third argument: for clock digits, pass `font_px(ctx, px, "0123456789:")`; for Chinese in an English UI, pass `font_px(ctx, px, "中")`.

```lua
-- Any size (8–96): the font the user picked; without a usable TTF fall back to a system font
local function font_px(ctx, px, sample)
  local font = ctx.fonts.size and ctx.fonts:size(px, sample)
  if font and font.px then return font end
  return px >= 28 and ctx.fonts.large or ctx.fonts.medium
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = g:size()
  local clock, title = font_px(ctx, 96, "0123456789:"), font_px(ctx, 30)
  local body, note = font_px(ctx, 24), font_px(ctx, 18)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(w // 2, 40, "12:30", { font = clock, align = "center" })
  local y = 40 + clock.line_height + 16       -- step down by line_height, not by the size
  g:text(24, y, "Today", { font = title })
  y = y + title.line_height + 8
  g:text(24, y, "Body text at 24", { font = body })
  y = y + body.line_height + 8
  g:text(24, y, "Page 3 of 12", { font = note })
end
```

Keep four points in mind:

- **Always measure widths; never hard-code them.** The user chooses the font, and the same sentence has a different width in a different font. Lay out with `font.line_height` and `font:measure()`, center with `align`, and wrap with `text_box`; never compute positions from the size number or from "how wide one CJK character is". Without a usable TTF, `font_px` falls back to a system font whose line height also differs from the size you requested.
- **Keep font objects in plain variables, not in `ctx.state`.** Calling `font_px` again with the same size returns the same object, so you do not need to cache it yourself.
- **The user decides the font**: on the device, the font is chosen under the toolbox's ⚙ (top right) → Font; if no font is chosen, it follows the reader's body font. Do not build a font picker into the app; when users want a different font, direct them to this setting. The Studio preview uses MiSans Regular by default, and you can upload your own TTF in the preview settings (the gear) to try it. To get the same result on a device, the user who installs the app must also choose that font on the device.
- **Opening a size for the first time reads the font from the storage card, which takes longer than drawing text.** A first frame that uses many sizes can exceed the 1500 ms budget of `on_draw`, and the app then exits: in `on_load`, call `ctx.budget:extend()` first, then call `font_px` once for each size you will use; see "Callback time budgets: extend before heavy work".

## Shrink the size when a line does not fit (auto-fit)

For a single line of variable length (a name, a title, a button, a number) that should be as large as possible within a fixed width and shrink when it does not fit, measure it with `font:measure` and try a few sizes in descending order. Copy this `fit_px` below the `font_px` from the first section:

```lua
-- Size ladder shared by the whole app. A session holds at most 32 size combinations;
-- stepping down one size at a time would use them up
local STEPS = { 30, 26, 24, 22, 20, 18, 16, 14 }

-- Try px first; if text does not fit, walk down the ladder and return the first font that fits max_w
local function fit_px(ctx, text, px, max_w)
  local font = font_px(ctx, px)
  if not font.px or font:measure(text) <= max_w then return font end  -- no TTF: cannot shrink
  for _, size in ipairs(STEPS) do
    if size < px then
      font = font_px(ctx, size)
      if font:measure(text) <= max_w then return font end
    end
  end
  return font  -- even the smallest step is too wide: shorten the text or wrap it with text_box
end

-- A name on a card: at most size 24, 200 wide, shrinks when it does not fit
local f = fit_px(ctx, item.name, 24, 200)
g:text(x, y, item.name, { font = f })
y = y + f.line_height + 4  -- lay out below with the line height of the font you actually got
```

- **Without a usable TTF, the text cannot shrink.** In that case `font_px` returns a system font (`font.px` is nil), and `fit_px` returns at the first step; the size does not change and no error is reported. Lay out with the returned font as usual.
- **Share one size ladder across the app and keep it short.** A session can hold at most 32 font-and-size combinations; beyond that, new sizes also fall back to system fonts silently.
- **Position elements based on the returned font.** Stack lines with `f.line_height` and center with `align`; do not hard-code line spacing from the size you requested.
- Paragraphs do not shrink: wrap them with `text_box`, and add `overflow = "ellipsis"` when they do not fit.

![Left: cards of the same width, a longer name drops to a size that fits; right: text_box wrapping, ellipsis and line spacing](/docs/text/fit-box-en.webp)

## Text larger than size 96: use an image

A TTF goes up to size 96. `font_px(ctx, 120)` cannot get size 120 and falls back to a system font, so the text becomes smaller instead. For text larger than 96, such as a large character on a cover or clock digits that fill the screen width, use an image:

1. Create an SVG asset: write the text in a `<text>` element, set the width and height to the display size (up to 800×800), and fill the text black. Studio converts it to XIC on import, so the device needs no font.
2. Draw it without `w` and `h`. Scaling uses nearest-neighbour sampling, and enlarging produces jagged edges.

**A single character** (a large 「读」 centred on a cover, 320×320, asset `cover_du`):

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="320" height="320" viewBox="0 0 320 320">
  <text x="160" y="160" font-size="300" font-family="KaiTi, STKaiti, serif" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="#000">读</text>
</svg>
```

```lua
function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w, h = g:size()
  g:clear(0)
  local big = ctx.package:image("cover_du")
  if big then
    g:image(big, (w - big.width) // 2, (h - big.height) // 2)
  end
end
```

**Changing digits** (a large clock): generate one asset for each character, `0`–`9` and the colon, all the same height, named `d0`…`d9` and `colon`, and draw them side by side:

```lua
local function glyph(ctx, ch)
  return ctx.package:image(ch == ":" and "colon" or ("d" .. ch))
end

-- Draw text (digits and colons only) centred on cx, top edge at y
local function draw_digits(ctx, g, text, cx, y)
  local images, total = {}, 0
  for i = 1, #text do
    local img = glyph(ctx, text:sub(i, i))
    if img then
      images[#images + 1] = img
      total = total + img.width
    end
  end
  local x = cx - total // 2
  for _, img in ipairs(images) do
    g:image(img, x, y)
    x = x + img.width
  end
end
```

- Studio renders the text into the image with the computer's fonts; the fonts installed on the device's card do not matter. List a few fonts in `font-family` and end with a generic family (`serif` or `sans-serif`) as a fallback.
- Give every digit image the same width, with the digit centred (`text-anchor="middle"`), so the string does not shift sideways when a digit changes.
- On a 480-wide screen, for `12:30` to fill the width, make each digit about 96 wide and the colon about 48.
- To refresh a clock face once a minute, see "Clock faces and countdowns".

## Alignment and centering

The `(x, y)` of `g:text(x, y, text, opts)` is an anchor. `align` is `left`, `center`, or `right`; `valign` is `top`, `middle`, `baseline`, or `bottom`. You do not need to measure the width to center text.

```lua
-- Button: the frame and the label share one center
local function button(g, x, y, w, h, label)
  g:rect(x, y, w, h, { radius = 8, line_width = 2 })
  g:text(x + w // 2, y + h // 2, label, { align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end
```

For buttons on ordinary screens such as settings and lists, use `ui:button` from `ctx.ui` instead of drawing them yourself; see "Ink Design".

For text that wraps, use `g:text_box(x, y, w, h, text, opts)`. It wraps text inside the rectangle; `overflow = "ellipsis"` ends the last line with `…` when the text does not fit, and `line_gap` adds space between lines.

```lua
g:text_box(24, 120, 432, 200, summary, {
  font = ctx.fonts.medium, line_gap = 6, overflow = "ellipsis",
})
```

## Italic, underline and strikethrough (2.28)

For text that needs to stand out, such as book titles, foreign words, links or old prices, add `italic`, `underline` or `strike` to `g:text` or `g:text_box`. They take effect only when the manifest `api` is at least `"2.28"`; older packages that set them are ignored and draw as before.

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.28"
local body = font_px(ctx, 24)
g:text(20, 100, "Dune", { font = body, italic = true })
g:text_box(20, 140, 440, 200, note, { font = body, underline = true })
g:text(20, 360, "Was 99", { font = body, strike = true })
```

- **Italic** shears each glyph to the right by about 18%, keeping the bottom fixed. Widths do not change: `measure` results and the wrapping of `text_box` and `layout` are the same as without it. The tops of glyphs can stick out past the measured width by up to about 18% of the glyph height, so leave room near the right edge. The system font and TTF fonts are both drawn this way; a font's own italic files are not used.
- **Underline** is drawn just below each line's baseline; **strikethrough** runs through the vertical middle of the line box. The line thickness follows the line height and the color matches the text.
- Each line is as long as the measured width of that line: spaces inside the line are underlined too, whitespace dropped at a wrap is not; a line with an ellipsis is underlined to the end of the ellipsis; a justified line is underlined across the full width. Each line counts as one drawing command.
- They combine freely with `bold`, `tabular` and with each other. `measure` and `layout` accept the three fields but do not read them.
- To italicize just one word in a sentence, measure the text before it with `measure` and draw the pieces with separate `g:text` calls. Mixing styles inside wrapped text is not supported.

## Measuring and paging

`font:measure(text)` returns the width of a single line, and `font.line_height` is the line height. `font:layout(text, w, h, opts)` lays out text by the `text_box` rules without drawing it; its third return value is the number of bytes that fit on the page. Use it for paging:

```lua
local function paginate(text, font, w, h)
  local pages, rest = {}, text
  while #rest > 0 do
    -- layout takes at most 65536 bytes per call; cut on a code point boundary
    local chunk = #rest > 65536 and rest:sub(1, utf8.offset(rest, 0, 65537) - 1) or rest
    local _, _, used = font:layout(chunk, w, h, { line_gap = 6 })
    if not used or used == 0 then break end
    pages[#pages + 1] = rest:sub(1, used)
    rest = rest:sub(used + 1)
  end
  return pages
end

-- In on_draw, draw page n with the same arguments used for paging
g:text_box(24, 80, 432, 640, pages[n], { font = ctx.fonts.medium, line_gap = 6 })
```

`measure` and `layout` do not draw, so you can also call them in `on_load`.

## Details of `ctx.fonts:size`

`font_px` is built on `ctx.fonts:size(px, sample)` (2.3; `sample` since 2.3.1):

- It tries the font the user chose in the system settings, then the reader's body font, and uses the first one that opens and can render the check characters. For the same `sample`, the same file is used for the whole session; `font.name` is its file name, and `font.px` equals `px`.
- `sample` is optional. When it is omitted, the check character depends on the system language (`ctx.i18n.locale`): 「国」 for Chinese, 「國」 for Traditional Chinese, 「あ国」 for Japanese, 「한」 for Korean, 「Ж」 for Russian, 「Ω」 for Greek, 「ก」 for Thai, one letter of the language for German, French, Spanish, and similar languages, and 「A」 for English and others. When the text is not in the system language, pass `sample`: `"0123456789:"` for a clock face, `"中"` for Chinese in an English UI. If you pass `sample`, the font must render every character in it (spaces do not count; at most 256 bytes).
- Without a usable TTF (the user has no fonts, the chosen file was deleted, or there is not enough TTF memory), it returns the system font with the closest line height. In that case `font.px` is nil, and the app runs as usual. The system allocates TTF memory; apps do not manage it.
- If `px` is not an integer from 8 to 96, it returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A session can use at most 32 different TTF sizes; later sizes return system fonts.
- TTF glyphs are centred vertically in the line box by their ink, so whichever font is in use, `valign = "middle"` and button labels sit in the middle.
- Characters missing from a TTF are drawn with a system font size that can render them (the size may differ from the surrounding text). They are drawn as boxes only when no system font has them either.

**Since 2.17, `ctx.fonts:installed` and `ctx.fonts:open` do not exist**, regardless of the version the package declares: calling them raises a Lua error; `ctx.capabilities.ttf` is false, so a package with `ttf` in `requires` does not open (`not_supported`); the manifest's `ttf_reserve_kb` is ignored, and you do not need to write it. Apps do not choose or list fonts; they only request sizes.

## Quick reference: what to use for what

| To draw | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Body text, buttons, lists | `font_px(ctx, 24)` (the system preset size; adjust it larger or smaller to suit the screen) |
| Titles | `font_px(ctx, 30)` (likewise; distinguish heading levels with different sizes) |
| Small text such as page numbers and notes, large text such as clocks and scores, any other size | `font_px(ctx, px)` (the font the user chose, at exactly the size you request) |
| Hand-drawn bitmap glyphs that you are switching to device fonts | `font_px(ctx, original size)` for each size, unchanged |
| Text larger than size 96: a large character on a cover, clock digits that fill the width | an image (see "Text larger than size 96") |
| A typeface specified by a designer, where glyph shapes must match exactly | render the text into image assets and draw them with `g:image` (see "Assets and drawing") |
| A single line of variable length (a name, title, button) that should shrink when it does not fit | `fit_px(ctx, text, px, max_w)` (see "Shrink the size when a line does not fit") |
| Long, changing CJK sentences | `font_px(ctx, 24)` + `text_box`; if the text does not fit, shorten it and add space |
| Text that needs to stand out: book titles, foreign words, links, old prices | `italic`, `underline`, `strike` (2.28, see "Italic, underline and strikethrough") |
| Letting the user change fonts | not implemented in the app; direct users to the toolbox's ⚙ → Font, or (2.27) after the user taps a button, open the font page directly with `ctx.system:open("settings.font")` |
