# 文字与字体

请先阅读第一节：需要任意字号时，使用 `font_px(ctx, px)`。它基于 `ctx.fonts:size`，支持 8–96 号的任意字号。字体由设备用户在系统中选择，应用不选择字体，因此字宽因用户而异：**宽度、居中、换行一律按实测计算，不要写死。** 第一节的代码只有几行，可以整段复制。一行文字放不下时需要自动缩小，见第二节。之后各节说明居中、分页和 `ctx.fonts:size` 的细节。

## 字体与字号怎么选（先看这里）

**规则：需要任意字号时，使用 `font_px(ctx, px)`。它使用用户选择的字体，支持 8–96 号的任意字号，应用不选择字体，也不查找字体文件。大于 96 号的文字做成图片，见下一节。**

正文 24 号、标题 30 号只是系统预设。游戏和视觉效果丰富的应用请使用不同大小的字体：醒目的大数字、逐级递进的标题、角落里的小注释，各自选用合适的字号。设计稿使用 14、18、20、26 号时，就照样写 `font_px(ctx, 14)` 等，不要归并成几个现成的档位。

![同一句话从 14 号到 96 号，以及用字号拉开层级的一页（Studio 预览实拍）](/docs/text/sizes-zh.webp)

把下面几行复制到 `main.lua` 中，之后需要字体时调用 `font_px(ctx, px)`。如果某个字号只用于绘制特定的字符，把这些字符写在第三个参数中：钟面数字写 `font_px(ctx, px, "0123456789:")`，英文界面中绘制中文写 `font_px(ctx, px, "中")`。

```lua
-- 任意字号（8–96）：用用户选的字体；没有可用的 TTF 时退回系统字体
local function font_px(ctx, px, sample)
  local font = ctx.fonts.size and ctx.fonts:size(px, sample)
  if font and font.px then return font end
  return px >= 28 and ctx.fonts.large or ctx.fonts.medium
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = g:size()
  local clock, title = font_px(ctx, 96, "0123456789:"), font_px(ctx, 30)
  local body, note = font_px(ctx, 24), font_px(ctx, 18)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(w // 2, 40, "12:30", { font = clock, align = "center" })
  local y = 40 + clock.line_height + 16       -- 往下排用 line_height，不用字号
  g:text(24, y, "今天", { font = title })
  y = y + title.line_height + 8
  g:text(24, y, "正文 24 号", { font = body })
  y = y + body.line_height + 8
  g:text(24, y, "第 3 页 / 共 12 页", { font = note })
end
```

注意以下四点：

- **宽度一律实测，不要写死。** 字体由用户选择，同一句话换一种字体，宽度就不同。排版使用 `font.line_height` 和 `font:measure()`，居中使用 `align`，折行使用 `text_box`；不要按字号或「一个汉字多宽」推算位置。没有可用的 TTF 时，`font_px` 退回系统字体，其行高也与所请求的字号不同。
- **字体对象保存在普通变量中，不放入 `ctx.state` 存档。** 以同一字号再次调用 `font_px` 返回的是同一个对象，无需自行缓存。
- **字体由用户决定**：在设备上，通过工具箱（「更多功能」）右上角的 ⚙ → 字体选择；未选择时，跟随阅读器的正文字体。不要在应用中制作选择字体的页面；用户需要更换字体时，引导他们到这里更换。Studio 预览默认使用 MiSans Regular，可以在预览设置（齿轮）中上传自己的 TTF 查看效果；要在设备上得到相同的效果，安装应用的用户也需要在设备上选择这款字体。
- **首次打开一个字号需要从存储卡读取字体，耗时远大于绘制文字。** 首帧同时用到很多字号时，容易超出 `on_draw` 的 1500 ms 预算，导致应用直接退出：在 `on_load` 中先调用 `ctx.budget:extend()`，再对每个要用的字号各调用一次 `font_px` 将其打开，见「回调时间预算：重计算前先 extend」。

## 一行放不下就降字号（字号自适应）

名字、标题、按钮、数值等长度不定的单行文字，如果要在固定宽度内尽量大、放不下时自动缩小，就用 `font:measure` 测量宽度，按几档字号依次往下尝试。把下面的 `fit_px` 复制到第一节的 `font_px` 之后：

```lua
-- 字号阶梯：整个应用共用这一组。一个会话最多 32 种字号组合，逐号往下减会把名额用光
local STEPS = { 30, 26, 24, 22, 20, 18, 16, 14 }

-- 先试 px，放不下就沿阶梯往下试，返回第一个能把 text 排进 max_w 的字体
local function fit_px(ctx, text, px, max_w)
  local font = font_px(ctx, px)
  if not font.px or font:measure(text) <= max_w then return font end  -- 没有 TTF 时缩不了
  for _, size in ipairs(STEPS) do
    if size < px then
      font = font_px(ctx, size)
      if font:measure(text) <= max_w then return font end
    end
  end
  return font  -- 最小一档也放不下：缩短文字，或改用 text_box 折行
end

-- 卡片里的名字：最大 24 号，宽 200，放不下自动缩小
local f = fit_px(ctx, item.name, 24, 200)
g:text(x, y, item.name, { font = f })
y = y + f.line_height + 4  -- 往下排跟着实际字体的行高走
```

- **没有可用的 TTF 时无法缩小。** 此时 `font_px` 返回系统字体（`font.px` 为 nil），`fit_px` 在第一档就返回，字号不变，也不报错；照常按返回的字体排版即可。
- **整个应用共用一组字号阶梯，档数不要过多。** 一个会话最多使用 32 种「字体 + 字号」组合，超出后新的字号也会静默退回系统字体。
- **位置按返回的字体计算。** 向下排列使用 `f.line_height`，居中使用 `align`，不要按原先请求的字号写死行距。
- 多行段落不通过缩小字号处理：使用 `text_box` 折行，放不下时加上 `overflow = "ellipsis"`。

![左：同样宽的卡片，名字越长自动降到放得下的一档；右：text_box 折行、省略号与行距](/docs/text/fit-box-zh.webp)

## 比 96 号更大的字：做成图片

TTF 最大为 96 号。`font_px(ctx, 120)` 无法得到 120 号，会退回系统字体，文字反而变小。封面大字、占满屏宽的钟面数字等大于 96 号的文字，做成图片：

1. 制作一张 SVG 素材：用 `<text>` 写入文字，宽高按显示尺寸确定（最大 800×800），文字填充为黑色。导入 Studio 时即转换为 XIC，设备上不需要字体。
2. 绘制时不写 `w`、`h`。缩放采用最近邻取样，放大后会出现锯齿。

**单个字符**（封面正中的「读」，320×320，素材名 `cover_du`）：

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="320" height="320" viewBox="0 0 320 320">
  <text x="160" y="160" font-size="300" font-family="KaiTi, STKaiti, serif" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="#000">读</text>
</svg>
```

```lua
function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w, h = g:size()
  g:clear(0)
  local big = ctx.package:image("cover_du")
  if big then
    g:image(big, (w - big.width) // 2, (h - big.height) // 2)
  end
end
```

**会变化的数字**（大字时钟）：为 `0`–`9` 和冒号各生成一张高度相同的素材，命名为 `d0`…`d9`、`colon`，绘制时按字符拼接：

```lua
local function glyph(ctx, ch)
  return ctx.package:image(ch == ":" and "colon" or ("d" .. ch))
end

-- 把 text（只含数字和冒号）水平居中画在 cx，顶边在 y
local function draw_digits(ctx, g, text, cx, y)
  local images, total = {}, 0
  for i = 1, #text do
    local img = glyph(ctx, text:sub(i, i))
    if img then
      images[#images + 1] = img
      total = total + img.width
    end
  end
  local x = cx - total // 2
  for _, img in ipairs(images) do
    g:image(img, x, y)
    x = x + img.width
  end
end
```

- 文字在 Studio 中渲染为图片，使用的是电脑上的字体，与设备存储卡上安装的字体无关。`font-family` 中列出几款字体，最后写一个通用字体族名（`serif` 或 `sans-serif`）作为兜底。
- 每张数字图使用相同的宽度，数字居中（`text-anchor="middle"`），这样数字变化时整串文字不会左右跳动。
- 屏宽为 480 时，`12:30` 要占满屏宽，每张数字图宽约 96，冒号宽约 48。
- 钟面如何按分钟刷新，见「钟面与倒计时」。

## 对齐与居中

`g:text(x, y, text, opts)` 的 `(x, y)` 是锚点：`align` 取 `left` `center` `right`，`valign` 取 `top` `middle` `baseline` `bottom`。居中无需自行测量宽度。

```lua
-- 按钮：框和字共用一个中心点
local function button(g, x, y, w, h, label)
  g:rect(x, y, w, h, { radius = 8, line_width = 2 })
  g:text(x + w // 2, y + h // 2, label, { align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end
```

设置页、列表等普通界面中的按钮无需自行绘制，使用 `ctx.ui` 的 `ui:button`，见「Ink Design 墨水屏设计规范」。

会换行的段落使用 `g:text_box(x, y, w, h, text, opts)`：在矩形内自动折行，`overflow = "ellipsis"` 在放不下时于末尾绘制 `…`，`line_gap` 用于增加行距。

```lua
g:text_box(24, 120, 432, 200, summary, {
  font = ctx.fonts.medium, line_gap = 6, overflow = "ellipsis",
})
```

## 斜体、下划线与删除线（2.28）

书名、外文词、链接、旧价这类需要区分的文字，给 `g:text` 或 `g:text_box` 加 `italic`、`underline`、`strike`。manifest 的 `api` 至少写 `"2.28"` 才生效；更早的包写了也被忽略，画面不变。

```lua
-- manifest: "api": "2.28"
local body = font_px(ctx, 24)
g:text(20, 100, "Dune", { font = body, italic = true })
g:text_box(20, 140, 440, 200, note, { font = body, underline = true })
g:text(20, 360, "旧价 99", { font = body, strike = true })
```

- **斜体**：字形向右错切约 18%，底部不动。宽度不变：`measure` 的结果、`text_box` 与 `layout` 的折行都和不写时一样。字顶可能伸出测量宽度，最多约字高的 18%，贴着右边缘时留出空间。系统字体和 TTF 都这样画，不用字体自带的斜体。
- **下划线**画在每行基线下方；**删除线**画在行盒的垂直中线。线粗随行高，颜色与文字相同。
- 线长等于这一行的测量宽度：行中空格也画线，折行处去掉的空白不画；带省略号的行画到省略号末尾；两端对齐的行画满宽度。每条线算一条绘图命令。
- 三者可以和 `bold`、`tabular` 以及彼此任意组合。`measure` 和 `layout` 接受这三个字段但不读取。
- 一段文字里只让一个词变斜体：用 `measure` 量出前面文字的宽度，分段调用 `g:text`。整段折行时混排多种样式目前不支持。

## 测量与分页

`font:measure(text)` 返回单行文字的宽度，`font.line_height` 是行高。`font:layout(text, w, h, opts)` 按 `text_box` 的规则排版但不绘制，第三个返回值是本页容纳的字节数，可用于分页：

```lua
local function paginate(text, font, w, h)
  local pages, rest = {}, text
  while #rest > 0 do
    -- layout 每次最多 65536 字节，切在码点边界上
    local chunk = #rest > 65536 and rest:sub(1, utf8.offset(rest, 0, 65537) - 1) or rest
    local _, _, used = font:layout(chunk, w, h, { line_gap = 6 })
    if not used or used == 0 then break end
    pages[#pages + 1] = rest:sub(1, used)
    rest = rest:sub(used + 1)
  end
  return pages
end

-- on_draw 里画第 n 页，参数与分页时相同
g:text_box(24, 80, 432, 640, pages[n], { font = ctx.fonts.medium, line_gap = 6 })
```

`measure` 和 `layout` 不进行绘制，也可以在 `on_load` 中调用。

## `ctx.fonts:size` 的细节

`font_px` 基于 `ctx.fonts:size(px, sample)`（2.3；`sample` 自 2.3.1 起）：

- 依次尝试用户在系统设置中选择的字体和阅读器的正文字体，取第一个能够打开且能渲染检查字符的字体。同一个 `sample` 在整个会话中固定使用同一个文件，`font.name` 是该文件的文件名，`font.px` 等于 `px`。
- `sample` 可以省略：省略时，检查字符随系统语言（`ctx.i18n.locale`）确定，中文为「国」、繁体中文为「國」、日文为「あ国」、韩文为「한」、俄文为「Ж」、希腊文为「Ω」、泰文为「ก」，德文、法文、西班牙文等使用本语言的一个字母，英文等为「A」。要显示的文字不属于系统语言时，传入 `sample`：钟面写 `"0123456789:"`，英文界面中绘制中文写 `"中"`。传入 `sample` 后，字体必须能渲染其中的每个字符（空格不计，最多 256 字节）。
- 没有可用的 TTF（用户未放入字体、所选文件被删除、TTF 内存不足）时，返回行高最接近的系统字体，此时 `font.px` 为 nil，应用照常运行。TTF 内存由系统分配，应用无需管理。
- `px` 不是 8–96 之间的整数时返回 `nil, "invalid_argument"`。一个会话最多使用 32 个不同的 TTF 字号，之后的字号返回系统字体。
- TTF 字形按墨迹在行盒中垂直居中，因此无论使用哪种字体，`valign = "middle"` 和按钮中的文字都位于正中。
- TTF 中缺少的字符，用系统字体中能渲染该字符的一个字号绘制（大小可能与前后文字不同）；系统字体中也没有时，才绘制为方框。

**自 2.17 起不再提供 `ctx.fonts:installed` 和 `ctx.fonts:open`**，与包声明的版本无关：调用它们会产生 Lua 错误；`ctx.capabilities.ttf` 为 false，`requires` 中包含 `ttf` 的包无法打开（`not_supported`）；manifest 中的 `ttf_reserve_kb` 会被忽略，无需填写。应用不选择字体、不列出字体，只按字号请求字体。

## 速查：画什么用什么

| 要绘制的内容 | 使用 |
| --- | --- |
| 正文、按钮、列表 | `font_px(ctx, 24)`（系统预设字号，可按画面调大或调小） |
| 标题 | `font_px(ctx, 30)`（同上；多级标题用不同字号区分层次） |
| 页码、注释等小字，钟面、计分等大字，以及其他任何字号 | `font_px(ctx, px)`（使用用户选择的字体，字号与请求一致） |
| 原先自绘的点阵字、位图字，改用设备字体 | 每个字号按原样写 `font_px(ctx, 原字号)` |
| 大于 96 号的文字：封面大字、占满屏宽的钟面数字 | 做成图片（见「比 96 号更大的字」） |
| 设计师指定的字体、字形必须完全一致 | 把文字做成图片素材，用 `g:image` 绘制（见「素材与绘图」） |
| 长度不定的单行文字（名字、标题、按钮），放不下时自动缩小 | `fit_px(ctx, text, px, max_w)`（见「一行放不下就降字号」） |
| 会变化的中文长句 | `font_px(ctx, 24)` + `text_box`；放不下时缩短文字、增加留白 |
| 书名、外文词、链接、旧价等需要区分的文字 | `italic`、`underline`、`strike`（2.28，见「斜体、下划线与删除线」） |
| 让用户更换字体 | 不在应用中实现；引导用户到工具箱 ⚙ → 字体，或（2.27）用户点按后 `ctx.system:open("settings.font")` 直接打开字体页 |
entries.example:
-- 任意字号（8–96）：用用户选的字体；没有可用的 TTF 时退回系统字体
local function font_px(ctx, px, sample)
  local font = ctx.fonts.size and ctx.fonts:size(px, sample)
  if font and font.px then return font end
  return px >= 28 and ctx.fonts.large or ctx.fonts.medium
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = g:size()
  local clock, title = font_px(ctx, 96, "0123456789:"), font_px(ctx, 30)
  local body, note = font_px(ctx, 24), font_px(ctx, 18)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(w // 2, 40, "12:30", { font = clock, align = "center" })
  local y = 40 + clock.line_height + 16       -- 往下排用 line_height，不用字号
  g:text(24, y, "今天", { font = title })
  y = y + title.line_height + 8
  g:text(24, y, "正文 24 号", { font = body })
  y = y + body.line_height + 8
  g:text(24, y, "第 3 页 / 共 12 页", { font = note })
end

entries.content:
# Callback time budgets: extend before heavy work

Every callback has a time limit: 2000 ms for `on_load`, 1500 ms for `on_draw`, and 1000 ms for all other callbacks. If a callback exceeds its limit, the app exits immediately: `on_leave` is not called, and `ctx.state` is not saved. Start any work whose duration is uncertain (AI thinking, simulation, offline settlement, bulk parsing, opening a batch of fonts for the first time) with one call to `ctx.budget:extend()`.

## The limits, and what a timeout does

| Callback | Limit | `extend`? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on_load` | 2000 ms | yes |
| `on_draw` | 1500 ms | yes |
| `on_input`, `on_tick`, `on_pause`, `on_resume` | 1000 ms | yes |
| `ctx:after` timer functions, network and dialog completion functions | 1000 ms | yes |
| `on_leave` | 1000 ms | no, returns `nil, "inactive"` |
| lock screen `on_load` + `on_draw` | 2000 ms together | no |

The limit is measured in wall-clock time from the start of the callback. Host functions such as opening a font, decoding an image, or reading or writing a file are not interrupted midway, but the time they take still counts, and the limit is checked at the next Lua instruction after they return.

A timeout error message contains `time budget`. Catching it with `pcall` has no effect: the host raises it again at the next instruction. A timeout ends the session in the same way as an uncaught error: the user sees the app exit suddenly, and the changes from this session are not saved.

On devices, callbacks are terminated mostly because of three patterns:

- computing inside `on_draw` (win rates, AI, laying out a whole book), which is more likely to time out as the screen becomes more complex;
- opening many TTF sizes for the first time in the first frame, each of which reads the font from the storage card;
- simulating offline earnings second by second, or parsing a large JSON in a single pass.

The Studio preview times callbacks against these limits and estimates Lua execution time at device speed. However, staying within the limit in the preview does not guarantee the same on the device. Handle any work close to the limit as described below.

## `ctx.budget:extend()`

```lua
local ok, err = ctx.budget:extend()
```

Moves the deadline of the current callback to 11 seconds after the call and returns `true`. However many times you call it, the deadline never goes past 30 seconds after the callback started. In `on_leave`, in a lock screen session, or outside a callback, it returns `nil, "inactive"`. The call itself takes almost no time and has no side effects when it is not needed, so call it whenever you are unsure.

There are three rules:

1. **Call it in the callback that does the work, before the work starts.** An extension applies only to the current callback: calling it in `on_input` leaves the next `on_draw` at 1500 ms.
2. **For work longer than 11 seconds, call it again every few seconds**, but a single callback still cannot run longer than 30 seconds; after that, it is terminated.
3. **Extending the deadline does not mean you can compute without limits.** While a callback runs, the screen does not update and keys are not handled, so the user sees the app freeze. Give the computation a duration the user can accept (typically 0.5–2 seconds for an AI move), and return the best result so far when it runs out.

## When you must use it

Start the following kinds of code with `ctx.budget:extend()`:

- **AI thinking**: search, minimax, Monte Carlo (such as poker win rates), pathfinding, several computer opponents acting in a row;
- **one-off batch work**: offline earnings settlement (see "Idle games and offline progress"), generating a level or map, simulating a whole game, precomputing a shuffled deck;
- **large data**: parsing or generating a large JSON, paginating a whole book, reading or writing several private files at once (see "When saves get large");
- **first use of resources**: opening several `ctx.fonts:size` sizes or decoding large images for the first time in `on_load` or the first frame (see "Text and fonts");
- **code (including AI-written code) whose loop length is uncertain**: whenever the loop count depends on the save, the player's progress, or random numbers, add the call.

It is not needed for ordinary key handling, drawing a normal screen, or changing a few state values.

## Example: an AI that keeps its own time

Run the thinking in `on_input` or a timer callback, not in `on_draw`. Extend first, then use `ctx.clock:millis()` to set a shorter budget for the computation, and return the best legal move when it runs out:

```lua
local function think(ctx, game)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  local stop = ctx.clock:millis() + 1500     -- our own budget: think for 1.5 s
  local best = first_legal_move(game)
  for depth = 1, 8 do
    local move = search(game, depth, stop)   -- returns nil once stop has passed
    if not move then break end
    best = move
  end
  return best                                -- still the best so far when time runs out
end
```

To keep the app responsive as well, show the player "Opponent is thinking" first: in the input callback, only change state and call `ctx:invalidate()`, then run the thinking in the next callback with `ctx:after(1, ...)`. That frame is presented first, so the user knows the app has not frozen.

## Example: Monte Carlo in chunks, the frame only reads the result

For a result that the screen displays but does not need immediately, such as a win rate, compute it in several chunks in timer callbacks, and extend at the start of each chunk as well. `on_draw` draws only the result already available, and draws "…" until the computation finishes. The screen and keys work as usual between chunks:

```lua
local job                                -- the computation in progress; replaced when the cards change

local function run(ctx)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  if not job then return end
  if equity_step(job, 100) then          -- 100 samples per chunk; true when done
    ctx.state.rate, job = job.rate, nil
    ctx:invalidate()
  else
    ctx:after(1, run)                    -- the next chunk runs in the next callback
  end
end

local function start(ctx, hand, board)
  job = equity_job(hand, board, 400)
  ctx.state.rate = nil
  ctx:after(1, run)
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local rate = ctx.state.rate
  g:text(20, 20, rate and (math.floor(rate * 100 + 0.5) .. "%") or "…")
end
```

Splitting the computation has another benefit: if a chunk times out, reduce the amount of work per chunk; the structure does not need to change.

## Example: open fonts in on_load

The first time a `ctx.fonts:size(px)` size is used, the host reads the font from the storage card, which takes far longer than drawing text. A first frame that uses a dozen sizes at once, plus the drawing itself, can easily exceed the 1500 ms of `on_draw`. Extend in `on_load` and open each size you need once. After that, the same size returns the same object, and drawing no longer incurs this cost:

```lua
local SIZES = { 16, 20, 24, 30, 48 }

function on_load(ctx)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  for _, px in ipairs(SIZES) do ctx.fonts:size(px) end
end
```

When a size that is not in the warm-up list appears for the first time, call `ctx.budget:extend()` in `on_draw` before opening it.

## Where you cannot extend

- `on_leave` has 1000 ms and cannot be extended: do only lightweight work on exit, and write large data in batches during normal operation (see "When saves get large").
- The two lock screen callbacks share 2000 ms and cannot be extended: the lock screen draws only what has already been computed.
- A single callback can run for at most 30 seconds: split longer work across multiple callbacks, and keep progress in `ctx.state` or a private file so the work can resume next time.

# 回调时间预算：重计算前先 extend

每个回调都有时间上限：`on_load` 为 2000 ms，`on_draw` 为 1500 ms，其余回调为 1000 ms。超出上限时，应用立即退出，`on_leave` 不会被调用，`ctx.state` 也不会保存。因此，凡是耗时无法确定的工作，例如 AI 思考、模拟、离线结算、批量解析、首次打开一批字体，都应在开始前调用一次 `ctx.budget:extend()`。

## 上限和超时的后果

| 回调 | 上限 | 能否 `extend` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on_load` | 2000 ms | 能 |
| `on_draw` | 1500 ms | 能 |
| `on_input`、`on_tick`、`on_pause`、`on_resume` | 1000 ms | 能 |
| `ctx:after` 的定时函数、网络和对话框的完成函数 | 1000 ms | 能 |
| `on_leave` | 1000 ms | 不能，返回 `nil, "inactive"` |
| 锁屏会话的 `on_load` + `on_draw` | 合计 2000 ms | 不能 |

上限按墙钟时间计算，从回调开始时计时。打开字体、解码图片、读写文件等宿主函数不会在执行中途被打断，但它们的耗时同样计入上限，并在其返回后的下一条 Lua 指令处检查。

超时错误的文本包含 `time budget`。用 `pcall` 捕获也无效，宿主会在下一条指令处再次抛出。超时与未捕获的错误一样会结束本次会话：用户看到应用突然退出，本次的修改也不会保存。

真机上被终止的回调大多来自以下三种写法：

- 在 `on_draw` 中执行计算（胜率、AI、整本书的排版），画面越复杂越容易超时；
- 首帧同时首次打开多个 TTF 字号，每个字号都需要从存储卡读取字体；
- 按秒循环模拟离线收益，或一次解析很大的 JSON。

Studio 预览按这些上限计时，并按设备速度估算 Lua 的耗时；但预览中未超时并不代表真机不会超时，接近上限的工作一律按下文的方法处理。

## `ctx.budget:extend()`

```lua
local ok, err = ctx.budget:extend()
```

将当前回调的截止时间改为调用时刻之后 11 秒，并返回 `true`；无论调用多少次，截止时间都不晚于回调开始后 30 秒。在 `on_leave`、锁屏会话中或回调之外调用时返回 `nil, "inactive"`。该调用本身几乎不耗时，在不需要时调用也没有副作用，因此无法确定时就调用。

规则共有三条：

1. **在执行工作的回调中、工作开始之前调用。** 延长只对当前这一次回调有效：在 `on_input` 中调用后，之后的 `on_draw` 仍为 1500 ms。
2. **超过 11 秒的工作，每隔几秒再调用一次**，但一次回调最长为 30 秒，超出后仍会被终止。
3. **延长不代表可以不限量地计算。** 回调运行期间，屏幕不会更新，按键也不会被处理，用户看到的是画面卡住。为计算设定一个用户可以接受的时长（AI 通常为 0.5～2 秒），到时交出当前最好的结果。

## 什么时候一定要用

编写以下代码时，在开头先调用 `ctx.budget:extend()`：

- **AI 思考**：搜索、极小极大、蒙特卡洛（例如扑克胜率）、寻路、多个电脑对手连续行动；
- **一次性批量工作**：离线收益结算（见「挂机与离线进度」）、生成关卡或地图、整局模拟、洗牌后预先计算整副牌；
- **大数据**：解析或生成大段 JSON、整本书的分页排版、一次读写多个私有文件（见「存档变大以后」）；
- **首次打开资源**：在 `on_load` 或第一帧中首次打开多个 `ctx.fonts:size` 字号、解码大图片（见「文字与字体」）；
- **AI 编写的代码、无法确定循环长度时**：只要循环次数取决于存档、玩家进度或随机数，就加上这一调用。

以下情况不需要：普通的按键处理、绘制一屏常规界面、修改几个状态值。

## 例子：AI 思考给自己定时

思考逻辑放在 `on_input` 或定时回调中，不放在 `on_draw` 中。先延长，再用 `ctx.clock:millis()` 为计算设定一个更短的预算，到时返回当前最好的合法着法：

```lua
local function think(ctx, game)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  local stop = ctx.clock:millis() + 1500     -- 自己的预算：思考 1.5 秒
  local best = first_legal_move(game)
  for depth = 1, 8 do
    local move = search(game, depth, stop)   -- 到了 stop 就返回 nil
    if not move then break end
    best = move
  end
  return best                                -- 时间到了也返回目前最好的
end
```

如果要兼顾响应，可以先让玩家看到「对手思考中」：在输入回调中只修改状态并调用 `ctx:invalidate()`，再通过 `ctx:after(1, ...)` 在下一次回调中执行思考。这样该帧会先上屏，用户可以知道应用没有卡死。

## 例子：蒙特卡洛分段算，画面只读结果

胜率这类需要在画面上显示、但不紧急的结果，分成几段放在定时回调中计算，每段开始前同样先延长；`on_draw` 只绘制已有的结果，尚未算完时绘制「…」。各段之间，画面和按键照常工作：

```lua
local job                                -- 进行中的计算；牌面变了就换一个

local function run(ctx)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  if not job then return end
  if equity_step(job, 100) then          -- 一次算 100 次抽样，算完返回 true
    ctx.state.rate, job = job.rate, nil
    ctx:invalidate()
  else
    ctx:after(1, run)                    -- 下一段放进下一次回调
  end
end

local function start(ctx, hand, board)
  job = equity_job(hand, board, 400)
  ctx.state.rate = nil
  ctx:after(1, run)
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local rate = ctx.state.rate
  g:text(20, 20, rate and (math.floor(rate * 100 + 0.5) .. "%") or "…")
end
```

拆分大计算的另一个好处是：某一段超时只与该段的长度有关，减少每段的计算次数即可，无需改动结构。

## 例子：在 on_load 里先打开字体

首次使用某个 `ctx.fonts:size(px)` 字号时，宿主需要从存储卡读取字体，耗时远大于绘制文字；首帧同时用到十几个字号时，加上画面本身的绘制，很容易超出 `on_draw` 的 1500 ms。在 `on_load` 中延长后，先把要用的字号各打开一次；之后同一字号返回同一个对象，绘制时不再产生这部分耗时：

```lua
local SIZES = { 16, 20, 24, 30, 48 }

function on_load(ctx)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  for _, px in ipairs(SIZES) do ctx.fonts:size(px) end
end
```

不在预热列表中的字号首次出现时，在 `on_draw` 中先调用 `ctx.budget:extend()`，再打开该字号。

## 延长不了的地方

- `on_leave` 只有 1000 ms，且不能延长：退出时只做轻量的工作，大块数据应在平时分批写好（见「存档变大以后」）。
- 锁屏会话的两个回调合计 2000 ms，且不能延长：锁屏只绘制已经计算好的内容。
- 一次回调最长为 30 秒：更长的工作拆分到多次回调中，进度记录在 `ctx.state` 或私有文件中，退出后下次继续执行。

# Ink Design: the e-ink design system

Ink Design is the first design system written for e-ink apps. It describes how to lay out, update, and interact with screens that are 1-bit, refresh slowly, and leave ghosting, on both key-only and touch devices. It is built on `ctx.ui`, the UI library that ships with the device. Every frame, you declare the widgets on the screen; the library draws them, hit-tests taps, moves key focus, and pages lists, while all values stay in your script. It follows the same model as Streamlit's full rerun and React's controlled components, and its layout uses the flexbox / grid vocabulary. This topic covers a quick start, layout, every widget, skins, and full-page examples. **Each widget comes with a picture rendered by the 2.x runtime (X4 Pro), followed by the exact code that drew it, which you can copy as a whole.** The UI library is an optional capability: write `"requires": ["ui"]` in the manifest, with an `"api"` of at least `"2.17"` (layout needs 2.15, text hierarchy 2.16).

## Overview: immediate-mode UI

The UI library uses **immediate mode**: there are no widget objects to create, mount, or destroy. On every `on_draw`, you state which widgets the screen has and what their values are. The library draws them immediately and records where each one is, so it can determine which widget the next tap or key press lands on.

| Concept | Streamlit | React | XTApp `ctx.ui` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| When it redraws | The whole script reruns on every interaction | The component re-renders when state changes | After `ctx:invalidate()`, `on_draw` runs again and declares the widgets again |
| Where state lives | `st.session_state` | `useState` | Plain script variables; put what must be saved in `ctx.state` |
| Widgets | `st.button()` | `<Button onClick>` | `ui:button(id, opts)` only declares; `ui:handle_event(ev)` returns what was pressed |
| Controlled values | `value=` | `value` + `onChange` | Pass `value`, `selected`, `text` every frame; update your variable on `change` |
| Layout | `st.columns` | flexbox / grid | `ui:row`, `ui:column`, `ui:grid`, `ui:stack`, with CSS terms |
| Identity | `key=` | `key` | `id`: unique within a frame; focus is tracked by `id` |

A screen consists of three pieces of code:

| Callback | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `on_load` | Call `ui = ctx.ui:create(opts)` once; get the font sizes you need |
| `on_draw` | `g:clear()` → `ui:begin_frame(g)` → declare widgets → `ui:end_frame()` |
| `on_input` | `local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)`; change state by `id` and `action`, then call `ctx:invalidate()` |

**When not to use it**: if the whole picture is your own drawing (a board, a map, cards), draw with `g`. If you only want "this area can be tapped and reached with the keys", use `ui:region` and keep drawing it yourself. You can mix the UI library and `g`: you can continue drawing before `begin_frame` and after `end_frame`.

## Principles: four rules for e-ink

E-ink has three constraints: it has only black and white; a frame takes about 0.5 s and changing screens leaves ghosting; and some devices have only arrow keys. Add that the screen size and the user's chosen font both change, and every rule in Ink Design follows from these four facts.

| Principle | Meaning | In code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Declare the screen every frame** | What is on screen is decided entirely by your script's variables; widgets hold no state | Declare every widget in `on_draw` and pass values each frame; on an action, change the variable and call `ctx:invalidate()` |
| **Design for refresh** | There is no animation and no pressed state; the feedback to a tap is the next frame. Large black areas ghost the most | Use mostly white; use solid black only for the main action and the selected item. Always use plain `ctx:invalidate()`, even when the screen or page changes; the system's automatic full refresh clears ghosting; page lists instead of scrolling them |
| **Positions from layout, lengths from the size table** | The screen size changes (landscape, future high-density screens), and so does the line height of the user's font. Hand-computed coordinates break or clip text when either changes | Read the size every frame with `local W, H = g:size()`; let `row` / `column` / `grid` / `stack` or `ui:layout` place things instead of computing `x` and `y`; take lengths only from the `S.*` entries of the "Size table"; derive control heights from the font (`S.control`, `h = "fit"`) |
| **One codebase, two devices** | The same screen works with only arrow keys and OK (Classic) and with direct taps (Pro) | Decide with `ctx.input.pointer`, not by device; make tap targets at least `S.hit` (44) square; arrow keys move focus by position, so an orderly layout produces the correct path |

The concrete lengths are in the next section, "Size table"; gray levels, type sizes, and refresh rules are collected in the last section, "Design rules: UI on e-ink".

## Size table: where every length comes from

Lengths in a screen have only two sources: the size table `S` below and the font's line height. The example code contains no other numbers. Define them once at the top of the file and share them across the app:

```lua
local S = {
  xs = 4, sm = 8, md = 16, lg = 24, xl = 40,   -- spacing
  margin = 16,                                 -- page margin
  radius = 8, radius_lg = 16,                  -- corner radius
  line = 2, line_bold = 3,                     -- line width
  hit = 44, bar = 16,                          -- smallest tap target, thin bar height
  tile = 96, tile_min = 132,                   -- tiles
  dialog_w = 400,                              -- widest dialog
}

function on_load(ctx)
  F = { big = ctx.fonts:size(40), title = ctx.fonts:size(30), body = ctx.fonts:size(24), small = ctx.fonts:size(20) }
  S.control = math.max(S.hit, F.body.line_height + 2 * S.sm)   -- height of one-line controls
end
```

| Name | Value (X4) | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `S.xs` | 4 | Two things that belong together: a label and its progress bar, a title and its subtitle, the inset of a list row |
| `S.sm` | 8 | Items in one group: menu rows, a set of radio options, two lines inside a card |
| `S.md` | 16 | Between controls: buttons side by side, form rows; text inset from a frame |
| `S.lg` | 24 | Between groups: sections of a settings page, a title and its content; inner padding of large frames such as dialogs and cards |
| `S.xl` | 40 | Smallest distance from a dialog to the screen edge |
| `S.margin` | 16 | Page margin: page content to the screen edge |
| `S.radius` / `S.radius_lg` | 8 / 16 | Controls, list rows / cards, dialogs |
| `S.line` / `S.line_bold` | 2 / 3 | Frames, focus rings / selected or focused cells, emphasis frames |
| `S.hit` | 44 | Smallest side of a tappable element |
| `S.bar` | 16 | Height of thin bars such as progress bars |
| `S.control` | body line height + 16, at least 44 (48 with the X4 default font) | Height of one-line controls: buttons, fields, tabs, steppers, pagers |
| `S.tile` / `S.tile_min` | 96 / 132 | Tile height / smallest column width for automatic columns |
| `S.dialog_w` | 400 | Widest a dialog gets: it fills a narrow screen and stops growing on a wide one |

Rules:

- **Spacing shows grouping**: things that belong together sit closer. Use `xs` / `sm` inside a group, `md` between controls, and `lg` between groups. A page with only one gap size does not show what belongs together.
- **Heights follow the font**: write `h = S.control` for one-line controls and `h = "fit"` for text; size multi-line content by its lines, such as `3 * F.body.line_height + 2 * S.sm` for a field or `F.body.line_height + S.xs + F.small.line_height + 2 * S.md` for a two-line row. When the user picks a larger font, the screen grows with it instead of clipping text.
- **Widths come from layout**: share space with `grow`, `"fit"`, `"1fr"`, percentages and `max_w` rather than fixed widths. Give changing numbers a `reserve` sized for the widest value.
- **Positions come from containers**: a top-level container uses `x = 0, y = 0, w = W` with `padding = S.margin` for the page margin; put a `spacer` in the page `column` to push things to the bottom. Only your own drawing needs coordinates, and `ui:layout` should compute its boxes first.
- **An element's own size does not scale with the screen**: radius, line width, tap targets and cell size are the same on every screen, so they are `S.*` values rather than proportions of the screen.
- To make the whole app looser or tighter, change only this table: everything moves together and nothing is missed.

Measurements of the device's own system screens (shelf, reader, keyboard and so on) are in the "Draw it yourself" sections later. They are reference values; your own app still uses this table.

## Quick start: your first screen

Below is a complete `index.lua` with three buttons: the main action "Save" is filled, "Cancel" is outlined, and "Delete" is disabled for now.

```lua widget=button
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local saved = false

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
ui:row("actions", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = {
  { kind = "button", id = "save", text = "Save", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, emphasis = true },
  { kind = "button", id = "cancel", text = "Cancel", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius },
  { kind = "button", id = "delete", text = "Delete", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, enabled = false },
} })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and id == "save" then saved = true end
```

As a runnable file, it looks like this. The size table `S` comes first, and `on_load` gets the fonts `F` and works out `S.control`, the height of one-line controls. Later code in this topic shows only its own part; the outer layer, `S` and `F` stay the same:

```lua
local ui, F

-- Size table (see "Size table" in the guide): take every length from here; write no other numbers
local S = {
  xs = 4, sm = 8, md = 16, lg = 24, xl = 40,   -- spacing: xs / sm inside a group, lg between groups
  margin = 16,                                 -- page margin
  radius = 8, radius_lg = 16,                  -- radius: controls / cards and dialogs
  line = 2, line_bold = 3,                     -- line width: frames / focus and emphasis
  hit = 44, bar = 16,                          -- smallest tap target, height of thin bars (progress)
  tile = 96, tile_min = 132,                   -- tiles: tile height, smallest column width when columns are automatic
  dialog_w = 400,                              -- widest a dialog gets
}

local saved = false

function on_load(ctx)
  F = { big = ctx.fonts:size(40), title = ctx.fonts:size(30), body = ctx.fonts:size(24), small = ctx.fonts:size(20) }
  -- height of one-line controls (buttons, fields, tabs): body line height plus padding, so it follows the user's font
  S.control = math.max(S.hit, F.body.line_height + 2 * S.sm)
  ui = ctx.ui:create()
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear()
  ui:begin_frame(g)
  local W, H = g:size()
  ui:row("actions", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = {
    { kind = "button", id = "save", text = "Save", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, emphasis = true },
    { kind = "button", id = "cancel", text = "Cancel", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius },
    { kind = "button", id = "delete", text = "Delete", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, enabled = false },
  } })
  ui:end_frame()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
  if action == "activate" and id == "save" then saved = true end
  if action then ctx:invalidate() return true end
  return false
end
```

```json
{ "api": "2.17", "app_id": "demo.buttons", "display_name": "Buttons", "version": "1.0.0", "requires": ["ui"] }
```

- The three buttons sit in a `ui:row`, and `grow = 1` splits the row evenly; the row's height is `"fit"`, the button height `S.control` plus the page padding. A wider or narrower screen, or a different font, needs no new numbers.
- Call `g:clear()` before `begin_frame`: the UI library does not clear the screen.
- The last two lines of `on_input` are the same on every screen: if the library returns an action, they redraw a frame and tell the host that the event was handled.
- To check whether the host has the UI library, use `if ctx.ui then … end`. A package whose `requires` lists `ui` installs only on devices that have it.
- Every item under "Widgets" in the Studio side panel is a runnable snippet like this, shown with its device frame. Click "Add to input", and the AI adapts it to your app.

## Frames, ids and limits

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| A frame | From `begin_frame(g)` to `end_frame()`. Calling `begin_frame` while the previous frame is open returns `nil, "busy"`; calling `end_frame` without `begin_frame` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` |
| Clearing | The library does not clear the screen; call `g:clear()` yourself before `begin_frame` |
| `id` | A non-empty string, unique within a frame. Focus and the field being edited are tracked by `id`, so give a widget the same `id` every frame |
| Position | Top-level widgets must have `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, with `w` and `h` at least 1; children of a container can omit them and let the container place them |
| Defaults | Font `ctx.fonts.medium`, color 15 (ink) |
| Limits | 128 widgets per frame and 16 levels of container nesting; beyond that, the call returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"` and the widget is not drawn. A composite widget counts as 1, plus 1 per part (a list counts only the rows on the current page) |
| Several UI objects | You can call `ctx.ui:create()` more than once, and each object keeps its own focus. For example, use one for the page and one for a pop-up menu: after the menu closes, the page's focus is where it was |

**Give each item in a list its own `id`**: build it in the loop, for example `"bag" .. i`, and parse it back on events (`tonumber(id:sub(4))`).

## Events and actions: handle_event

`ui:handle_event(ev)` passes one input event to the UI library and returns `id, action, v`. For an event that isn't meant for the library, it returns `nil, nil`, and you handle the event yourself.

| Input | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` down | Focused widget, `press` (informational; no handling needed) |
| `ok` up, focus unchanged | Focused widget, `activate` |
| Arrow keys | Focus moves to the nearest widget in that direction, `focus` |
| Tap, double tap | The tapped widget, `activate`; focus moves to it. A double tap is two `activate`s |
| Hold | The touched widget, `long_press` |
| `activate` on a field | Editing starts, `edit` |
| A composite part changes value | `change`, `v` is the new value |

`v` for composite widgets:

| Widget | `v` on `activate` / `focus` | `v` on `change` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs`, `radio` | Item index | Newly selected index (when the tapped item isn't the current one) |
| `stepper` | 1 is minus, 2 is plus | The new value (kept within `min`, `max`) |
| `pager` | 1 is previous, 2 is next | `page - 1` or `page + 1` |
| `list` | Data row index (not the row on the page) | The new page when keys move past the page |

**The library stores no values**: if you don't update your variable on `change`, the next frame draws the old value. This is what a controlled component is:

```lua
function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
  if id == "size" and action == "change" then size = v end          -- stepper
  if id == "cat" and action == "change" then tab = v; ctx:invalidate() return true end  -- new tab
  if action == "activate" and id == "wifi" then s.wifi = not s.wifi end  -- a switch flips itself
  if action then ctx:invalidate() return true end
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "back" and ev.phase == "down" then … end  -- keys the library doesn't use
  return false
end
```

- Disabled widgets (`enabled = false`) return no action, and a tap on them doesn't pass through to the widget below.
- `long_press` is suitable for "more actions", for example holding a book to delete or share it.

## Focus, keys and touch

X4 Classic has only keys; X4 Pro has keys and touch. The same code must be fully usable on both. The library manages focus for you:

| Case | Focus |
| --- | --- |
| Whether it is drawn | Drawn only under key input. Devices without touch always draw it; touch devices draw it after a key press and hide it after a tap (focus is kept, and the next key press starts from it) |
| First frame | The first focusable widget |
| The focused widget isn't declared this frame | The first widget |
| The focused widget is disabled | The nearest enabled widget |
| Arrow keys | Finds the widget in that direction by position: overlap on the other axis first, then distance, then declaration order. Focus doesn't wrap around |
| Explicit routes | `nav = { up = "id", down = "id", left = "id", right = "id" }` on a widget overrides the position search |
| Keeping keys away | Set `enabled = false`, or don't declare the widget this frame |

Focusable: `button`, `switch`, `field`, `region`, and the parts of composite widgets. `label`, `image`, and `progress` are not focusable.

**When you return from a sub-page, focus returns to the button that opened it** (2.7):

```lua
local back_to = {}           -- one entry per level, like browser history

local function open(screen_name)
  back_to[#back_to + 1] = ui:focused()
  screen = screen_name
end

local function close()
  screen = "home"
  ui:focus(table.remove(back_to))   -- next frame, focus is back on that button
end
```

The `part` in `ui:focus(id, part)` is the item index of a composite widget, for example the 3rd row of a list.

**No pressed state**: an e-ink frame takes about 0.5 s and a tap only 0.2 s, so a "pressed" frame is never seen and costs an extra refresh. The feedback for a tap is the frame after `activate`, so call `ctx:invalidate()` immediately after `activate`.

## Layout: containers and children (2.15)

`ui:row` and `ui:column` are flexbox, `ui:grid` is CSS grid, and `ui:stack` layers its children. A container places its `children`, so children need no coordinates. Only packages with manifest `api` ≥ 2.15 use this layout.

```lua
local s = { wifi = true }    -- the table that holds your state
local W, H = g:size()
ui:column("page", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = H, padding = S.margin, gap = S.lg, children = {
  { kind = "label", id = "title", text = "Settings", font = F.title, h = "fit" },
  { kind = "switch", id = "wifi", text = "Wi-Fi", h = "fit", selected = s.wifi },
  { kind = "spacer" },                                   -- pushes the button to the bottom
  { kind = "button", id = "ok", text = "Done", h = S.control, emphasis = true },
} })
```

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `{ kind = "button", id = …, … }` | A child: `kind` is the widget name, and the other fields are the same as when calling `ui:button` |
| `kind = "row"` / `"column"` / `"grid"` / `"stack"` | Children can also be containers, up to 16 levels deep |
| `{ kind = "spacer" }` | Empty space with `grow = 1`; not counted toward the 128 widgets |
| `false` | A `false` in `children` is skipped, which lets you write `cond and {…}` |
| `hidden = true` | The child is neither placed nor drawn; the following children close the gap |
| Top-level container | Must have `id`, `x`, `y`; `w` and `h` are numbers or `"fit"`, not percentages. For a full screen, write `w = W, h = H` (from `g:size()`), not `480` and `800` |

**Container fields**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `padding` | Inner padding, CSS shorthand with 1–4 numbers: `S.margin`, `{ S.sm, S.margin }`, `{ top, right, bottom, left }` |
| `gap`, `row_gap`, `column_gap` | Space between children |
| `justify_content` | Main axis: `start`, `center`, `end`, `space_between`, `space_around`, `space_evenly` |
| `align_items` | Cross axis: `stretch` (default), `start`, `center`, `end`, `baseline` |
| `wrap`, `align_content` | Whether to wrap when children don't fit, and how the lines are distributed |
| `divider` | Lines between neighboring children: `{ line_width, color, inset }` |
| `border`, `line_width`, `border_color`, `radius` | Outer frame |
| `background` | Shade 0–15, drawn as dots; see "Design rules" |
| `skin` | A skin as the background; see "Skins" |

**Child fields**

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `w`, `h` | A number, `"fit"` (content size), or `"40%"` (a share of the container's inner box) |
| `min_w`, `max_w`, `min_h`, `max_h` | Size limits; `min` defaults to 1 |
| `aspect_ratio` | Width over height, for example `2 / 3` for a cover |
| `grow`, `shrink` | Share the spare space; shrink in proportion when children don't fit |
| `align_self`, `justify_self` | Alignment for this child only |
| `column_span`, `row_span` | Number of cells spanned in a grid |

Only `label`, `button`, `switch`, `tabs`, `image`, `spacer`, and containers accept `"fit"`. A `button`'s content width is the text width plus 24, and its height is the line height plus 16 (that is `2 * S.sm`, like `S.control` but without the 44 minimum); a `switch` grows when it has a `note`. The other widgets (`field`, `radio`, `stepper`, `pager`, `list`, `progress`, `region`) have no content size: give them a numeric height or share space with `grow` in a `column`.

## Layout: rows and columns

```lua widget=row_toolbar
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
-- in a real page the footer sits at the bottom (a spacer in the page column, or y = H - height); here the two bars sit together so both are visible
ui:column("bars", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", gap = S.lg, children = {
  { kind = "row", padding = { S.sm, S.margin }, gap = S.md, align_items = "center", children = {
    { kind = "button", id = "back", text = "Back", w = "fit", h = S.control, radius = S.radius },
    { kind = "label", id = "title", text = "Chapter 3", font = F.title, bold = true, grow = 1, align = "center" },
    { kind = "button", id = "menu", text = "Index", w = "fit", h = S.control, radius = S.radius },
  } },
  { kind = "row", h = S.control, padding = { 0, S.margin }, align_items = "center", children = {
    { kind = "label", id = "pct", text = "38%", font = F.small, w = "fit", tabular = true, reserve = "100%" },
    { kind = "spacer" },
    { kind = "label", id = "time", text = "21:40", font = F.small, w = "fit", tabular = true, reserve = "88:88" },
  } },
} })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and id == "back" then go_back = true end
```

Top bars, bottom bars, and button strips are `row`s: the title takes the remaining width with `grow = 1`, and the buttons on either side use `w = "fit"`, sized to their text.

```lua widget=column_card

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
```

A settings group is a `column`: `border` + `radius` form the card, `divider` draws lines between items, and `h = "fit"` lets the card grow with its content.

```lua widget=grid_menu
ui:grid("menu", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, columns = { min = S.tile_min },
  auto_rows = S.tile, gap = S.md, children = {
```

`columns` can also be a track list: a number is a fixed width, `"fit"` is the content width, `"1fr"` shares the remaining width, and `"30%"` is a proportional share. Use `"fit"` for a form's label column: it takes the width of the longest label and stays aligned in any language or size. `column_span = 3` spans the whole row.

## Layout: stacks and shades

```lua widget=stack_cover
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

local function draw_art(g, r)
  g:pattern(r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h, { kind = "line", density = 25 })
  local tw = F.title:measure("Cover") + 2 * S.md
  local th = F.title.line_height + 2 * S.sm
  g:rect(r.x + (r.w - tw) // 2, r.y + (r.h - th) // 2, tw, th, { fill = true, color = 0, radius = S.radius })
  g:text(r.x + r.w // 2, r.y + r.h // 2, "Cover", { font = F.title, align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
ui:column("page", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, children = {
  { kind = "stack", id = "cover", aspect_ratio = 16 / 9, border = true, radius = S.radius_lg, padding = S.md, children = {
    { kind = "region", id = "art", draw = draw_art },
    { kind = "button", id = "tag", text = "New", font = F.small, w = "fit", h = "fit", emphasis = true, radius = S.radius, justify_self = "end", align_self = "start" },
  } },
} })
```

Children of a `stack` share one area; later children are on top and are hit first. `justify_self` and `align_self` pin each child to a corner. `aspect_ratio` derives a cover's height from its width, so it keeps its shape on any screen.

```lua widget=dither_bg
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
ui:column("page", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.lg, children = {
  -- dark dots are for blocks only (covers, banners), never under text
  { kind = "column", h = 2 * S.control, background = 10, radius = S.radius_lg, children = {} },
  -- for text on a tone, put the text on paper and let the dots frame it: it stays clear at any size
  { kind = "column", h = "fit", background = 4, radius = S.radius_lg, padding = S.sm, children = {
    { kind = "column", h = "fit", background = 0, radius = S.radius, padding = S.md, gap = S.xs, children = {
      { kind = "label", id = "tip_t", text = "Tip", font = F.body, bold = true, h = "fit" },
      { kind = "label", id = "tip_b", text = "Text sits on paper; the dots only frame it", font = F.small, h = "fit" },
    } },
  } },
} })
```

## Layout: rects only with ui:layout

`ui:layout(rect, spec)` uses the same rules to compute rects only: it draws nothing, registers no widget, doesn't count toward the 128 widgets, and works inside or outside a frame. Use it to place your own drawing (a board, a chart) on the same grid as the UI library:

```lua
local W, H = g:size()
local box = ui:layout({ x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = H }, { kind = "column", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = {
  { id = "head", h = S.control },
  { id = "board", grow = 1 },
  { id = "foot", h = S.control },
} })
draw_board(g, box.board.x, box.board.y, box.board.w, box.board.h)
```

- The result has `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`; `[1..n]` are the children's boxes, and children with an `id` are also stored at `[id]`.
- If children overflow the container, the result has `overflow` (the index of the first child that overflows). The library doesn't clip; the overflowing part is drawn as is.
- A child without `kind` is an empty box. A layout can have up to 1024 children.
- You can also measure before declaring: when a list takes `grow = 1`, call `ui:layout` with the same `children` first, read the height the list gets, work out rows per page and the page count, then declare the screen (see "Full-page example: shop").

**Differences from CSS**

| Rule | UI library | CSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimum size | `min_w` and `min_h` default to 1: items shrink, and text is cut with an ellipsis | `auto`, not smaller than the content |
| `grow` basis | Shares from 0 | `flex-basis` |
| Minimum of `fr` | 0 | Content width |
| Sizes | Whole pixels only | Can be fractional |
| `margin` | Not supported; use `gap` and `padding` | Supported |

Exception: a `label`, `button`, `switch`, or `tabs` in a `row` or `column` without a numeric height keeps at least one line of text, and overflows rather than squashing the text out of view.

## Button ui:button

```lua widget=button
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local saved = false

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
ui:row("actions", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = {
  { kind = "button", id = "save", text = "Save", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, emphasis = true },
  { kind = "button", id = "cancel", text = "Cancel", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius },
  { kind = "button", id = "delete", text = "Delete", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, enabled = false },
} })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and id == "save" then saved = true end
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `font`, `bold`, `tabular` | The label; `font_min` is the smallest size to shrink to before the text is cut |
| `radius`, `border` | Corner radius; whether to draw the frame |
| `emphasis` | Main action, filled. At most one per screen |
| `selected` | Selected (inverted), for the current item of a menu |
| `enabled` | When `false`, the button is covered with white dots and is neither tappable nor focusable |
| `align` | Text alignment: `left`, `center` (default), `right` |
| `badge` | A small badge at the top right: a number or a short word |
| `image` | Icon button; cannot be combined with `skin` |
| `skin`, `nav` | Skin, key routes |

States in order of priority, from highest: disabled > selected (fill 15, text 0) > emphasis (filled; focus adds a ring outside) > focused (filled) > normal (outlined).

A button's text area is the whole button, with no side padding: text with `align = "left"` touches the frame, and a badge covers long text. So a column of selectable menu rows is not built from buttons; draw the rows with `ui:list` and keep the text `S.md` from the edge:

```lua widget=button_menu
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local folders = { { "Inbox", "3" }, { "Drafts", "12" }, { "Sent" } }
local cur = 2

local function draw_folder(g, r, f, st)
  local ink = 15
  if st.selected then
    g:rect(r.x, r.y + S.xs, r.w, r.h - 2 * S.xs, { fill = true, radius = S.radius })
    ink = 0
  elseif st.focused then
    g:rect(r.x, r.y + S.xs, r.w, r.h - 2 * S.xs, { radius = S.radius, line_width = S.line })
  end
  local mid = r.y + r.h // 2
  g:text(r.x + S.md, mid, f[1], { font = F.body, color = ink, valign = "middle" })
  if f[2] then   -- the count sits right-aligned on the text line, not on the corner
    g:text(r.x + r.w - S.md, mid, f[2], { font = F.small, color = ink, align = "right", valign = "middle", tabular = true })
  end
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
local row_h = S.control + 2 * S.xs
ui:column("menu", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, children = {
  { kind = "list", id = "folders", h = #folders * row_h, row_h = row_h, count = #folders, page = 1, selected = cur,
    draw = function(g, r, i, st) draw_folder(g, r, folders[i], st) end },
} })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and id == "folders" then cur = v end
```

| --- | --- |

## Text field ui:field

```lua widget=field
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local title = "Dune"
local note = ""

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
ui:column("form", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = {
  { kind = "field", id = "title", h = S.control, text = title, placeholder = "Title", max_chars = 32,
    radius = S.radius, enter = "next", on_change = function(ctx, t) title = t end },
  { kind = "field", id = "note", h = 3 * F.body.line_height + 2 * S.sm, text = note, placeholder = "Write a note…", multiline = true,
    radius = S.radius, enter = "done", on_change = function(ctx, t) note = t end },
} })
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | The current text, passed every frame; the library doesn't store it |
| `on_change(ctx, text)` | Called on every edit: store the text and pass it in the next frame |
| `on_end(ctx, text)` | Called when editing ends |
| `placeholder` | Hint text shown while the field is empty (color 8) |
| `max_chars` | Maximum number of characters |
| `kind` | `text`, `number`, `secret` (drawn as `*`), `letters` (URLs, accounts) |
| `multiline` | Multiple lines |
| `enter` | The confirm key: `done`, `save`, `next` (jump to the next field), `search`, `newline` (requires `multiline`) |

- A tap, or `ok` while the field is focused, starts editing, and `handle_event` returns `edit`. The system keyboard docks at the bottom of the screen and takes `ctx.input.keyboard_h` pixels (340 on X4 Pro); place the field being edited and the buttons to press above it.
- `ui:stop_edit()` ends editing and returns the text (without calling `on_end`), e.g. when "Save" is tapped; `ui:editing()` returns the `id` being edited.
- You don't need to dismiss the keyboard when switching screens: if the field being edited isn't declared this frame, editing ends automatically.
- On devices without touch, `keyboard_h` is 0, and input falls back to full-screen entry. A disabled field can't start editing.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `items` | 1–64 names |

## Paged list ui:list

```lua widget=list
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local books = { "Dune", "Emma", "Ulysses", "Beloved", "Hamlet", "Walden", "Lolita", "Persuasion", "Middlemarch" }
local page, pick = 1, 2

local function draw_row(g, r, text, st)
  local ink = 15
  if st.selected then
    g:rect(r.x, r.y + S.xs, r.w, r.h - 2 * S.xs, { fill = true, radius = S.radius })
    ink = 0
  elseif st.focused then
    g:rect(r.x, r.y + S.xs, r.w, r.h - 2 * S.xs, { radius = S.radius, line_width = S.line })
  end
  g:text(r.x + S.md, r.y + r.h // 2, text, { font = F.body, color = ink, valign = "middle" })
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
local per = 4                                  -- rows per page: chosen for the content, not to fill the screen
local row_h = S.control + 2 * S.xs
local pages = math.max(1, (#books + per - 1) // per)
ui:column("shelf", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.sm, children = {
  { kind = "list", id = "books", h = per * row_h, row_h = row_h, count = #books, page = page, selected = pick,
    draw = function(g, r, i, st) draw_row(g, r, books[i], st) end },
  { kind = "pager", id = "pg", h = S.control, page = page, pages = pages },
} })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "change" then
  page = v
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end
if action == "activate" and id == "books" then pick = v end
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `count` | Total number of rows |
| `row_h` | Row height; `h // row_h` rows per page |
| `page` | The current page (kept by the script) |
| `selected` | The selected row |
| `draw(g, r, i, st)` | Draws one row: `r` is the row's box, `i` is the row index, and `st` has `selected`, `focused`, `enabled` |

Tapping a row returns `activate` with its index. Pressing down on the last row of the page returns `change` with the next page, and pressing up on the first row returns the previous page: update `page`, and focus lands on the first or last row of the new page. On e-ink, lists **page instead of scrolling**; paging also calls plain `ctx:invalidate()`.

Write the list height as rows-per-page × row height and count the pages from the same number, so the list and the pager agree. When the list takes the spare height with `grow = 1`, rows per page vary with the screen: measure the list with `ui:layout` first, then count the pages.

```lua widget=list_detail
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local notes = {
  { "Ch. 1 · Beginnings", "12 notes" },
  { "Ch. 2 · Far away", "3 notes" },
  { "Ch. 3 · Return", "8 notes" },
  { "Ch. 4 · Epilogue", "1 note" },
}
local open_chapter

local function draw_note(g, r, n, st)
  local x, w = r.x + S.md, r.w - 2 * S.md
  -- centre both lines in the row: add the title, gap and note heights, then split from the middle
  local block = F.body.line_height + S.xs + F.small.line_height
  local top = r.y + (r.h - block) // 2
  if st.focused then g:rect(r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h, { radius = S.radius, line_width = S.line }) end
  g:text(x, top, n[1], { font = F.body, bold = true })
  g:text(x, top + F.body.line_height + S.xs, n[2], { font = F.small })
  g:text(x + w, r.y + r.h // 2, ">", { font = F.body, align = "right", valign = "middle" })
  g:rect(x, r.y + r.h - 1, w, 1, { fill = true })
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
local row_h = F.body.line_height + S.xs + F.small.line_height + 2 * S.md   -- two lines plus padding
ui:column("toc", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, children = {
  { kind = "list", id = "notes", h = #notes * row_h, row_h = row_h, count = #notes, page = 1,
    draw = function(g, r, i, st) draw_note(g, r, notes[i], st) end },
} })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and id == "notes" then open_chapter = v end
```

You draw what a row looks like; the library handles only hit-testing, focus, and paging.

## Custom area ui:region

```lua widget=region_slots
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local bag = { "S", "D", "P", false, "K", false, "B", false, false }
local pick = 1

local function draw_slot(g, r, item, st)
  if st.selected then
    g:rect(r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h, { fill = true, radius = S.radius })
  else
    g:rect(r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h, { radius = S.radius, line_width = st.focused and S.line_bold or S.line })
  end
  if item then
    g:text(r.x + r.w // 2, r.y + r.h // 2, item, { font = F.title, color = st.selected and 0 or 15, align = "center", valign = "middle" })
  end
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
local cell = S.tile                            -- cell size: the element's own size, the same on any screen
local cells = {}
for i = 1, #bag do
  cells[i] = { kind = "region", id = "bag" .. i, selected = pick == i,
    draw = function(g, r, st) draw_slot(g, r, bag[i], st) end }
end
ui:grid("bag", { x = S.margin, y = S.margin, w = "fit", h = "fit", columns = { cell, cell, cell },
  auto_rows = cell, gap = S.sm, children = cells })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and id:sub(1, 3) == "bag" then pick = tonumber(id:sub(4)) end
```

`ui:region(id, { x, y, w, h, draw = function(g, r, st) … end })` is an area that can be tapped and reached with the keys, and you draw how it looks. `st` has `focused`, `selected`, `enabled`; an error inside `draw` is raised from `end_frame`. Inventories, board cells, calendars, and cards all use it. It also accepts `selected`, `enabled`, `nav`, and `badge`.

## Skins: nine-slice images

`ctx.ui:create{ skins = { … } }` registers skins on a UI object: an image stretched as a nine-slice and used as the background of buttons, containers, and custom rows.

```lua widget=skin_button

-- on_load
ui = ctx.ui:create({ skins = {
  iron = { image = ctx.package:image("frame"), edge = 12, pad = { S.sm, S.md },
    focused = { image = ctx.package:image("frame_on"), text_color = 0 },
    selected = { image = ctx.package:image("frame_on"), text_color = 0 },
    emphasis = { image = ctx.package:image("frame_on"), text_color = 0 } },
} })

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
ui:column("trade", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = "fit", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = {
  { kind = "row", gap = S.md, children = {
    { kind = "button", id = "buy", text = "Buy", grow = 1, h = S.control, skin = "iron", emphasis = true },
    { kind = "button", id = "sell", text = "Sell", grow = 1, h = S.control, skin = "iron" },
  } },
  { kind = "button", id = "exchange", text = "Exchange (locked)", h = S.control, skin = "iron", enabled = false },
} })
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `image` | Required, `ctx.package:image("key")` |
| `edge` | Width of the corners that don't stretch, CSS shorthand with 1–4 numbers (0–255) |
| `pad` | Distance from the text to the edge, `edge` by default |
| `text_color` | Text color, 15 by default |
| `focused`, `selected`, `disabled`, `emphasis` | Image and text color for each state: `{ image = …, text_color = … }` |

States you don't configure are derived: disabled = normal plus white dots, selected = inverted, focused = normal plus a ring, and emphasis isn't drawn unless configured. A skin draws with at most 9 commands.

```lua widget=skin_list
-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
```

In custom widgets, `ui:skin(g, name, x, y, w, h, st)` draws the same skin and returns the text color and text box `tc, tx, ty, tw, th`, so list rows and cells can match the buttons.

## Full page: shop

```lua widget=page_shop
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local goods = {
  { "Bread", 12 }, { "Potion", 40 }, { "Rope", 8 }, { "Lamp", 25 },
  { "Map", 60 }, { "Rations", 15 }, { "Torch", 6 }, { "Cloak", 90 },
  { "Pot", 30 }, { "Rod", 45 }, { "Blanket", 35 }, { "Compass", 70 },
}
local tab, page, pick, qty, money = 1, 1, 2, 1, 120


local function draw_good(g, r, item, st)
  local ink = 15
  if st.selected then g:rect(r.x, r.y + S.xs, r.w, r.h - 2 * S.xs, { fill = true, radius = S.radius }) ink = 0
  elseif st.focused then g:rect(r.x, r.y + S.xs, r.w, r.h - 2 * S.xs, { radius = S.radius, line_width = S.line }) end
  g:text(r.x + S.md, r.y + r.h // 2, item[1], { font = F.body, color = ink, valign = "middle" })
  g:text(r.x + r.w - S.md, r.y + r.h // 2, item[2] .. "G", { font = F.body, color = ink, align = "right", valign = "middle", tabular = true })
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
local price = goods[pick][2] * qty
local row_h = S.control + 2 * S.xs
local function shop(page_now, pages)
  return {
    { kind = "row", align_items = "center", gap = S.md, children = {
      { kind = "label", id = "title", text = "General store", font = F.title, bold = true, grow = 1 },
      { kind = "label", id = "money", text = money .. "G", font = F.body, w = "fit", tabular = true, reserve = "9999G" },
    } },
    { kind = "tabs", id = "cat", h = S.control, items = { "All", "Food", "Tools" }, value = tab, gap = S.xs, radius = S.radius },
    { kind = "list", id = "goods", grow = 1, row_h = row_h, count = #goods, page = page_now, selected = pick,
      draw = function(g, r, i, st) draw_good(g, r, goods[i], st) end },
    { kind = "row", gap = S.md, align_items = "center", children = {
      { kind = "stepper", id = "qty", w = 4 * S.control, h = S.control, value = qty, min = 1, max = 9 },
      { kind = "spacer" },
      { kind = "pager", id = "pg", w = 2 * S.control, h = S.control, page = page_now, pages = pages, text = "" },
    } },
    { kind = "button", id = "buy", h = S.control, radius = S.radius, emphasis = true, enabled = money >= price,
      text = "Buy · " .. price .. "G" },
  }
end
-- the list takes the spare height (grow = 1), so rows per page vary: measure it with ui:layout first, then count the pages
local box = ui:layout({ x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = H }, { kind = "column", padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = shop(1, 1) })
local per = math.max(1, box[3].h // row_h)
local pages = math.max(1, (#goods + per - 1) // per)
page = math.min(page, pages)
ui:column("shop", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = H, padding = S.margin, gap = S.md, children = shop(page, pages) })

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "change" then
  if id == "cat" then tab, page = v, 1
  elseif id == "qty" then qty = v
  else page = v end
  ctx:invalidate() -- tabs and paging use a plain refresh too
  return true
elseif action == "activate" then
  if id == "goods" then pick = v
  elseif id == "buy" then money = money - goods[pick][2] * qty end
end
```

Tabs + paged list + stepper + pager + main button. The list takes the middle height with `grow = 1`, so how many rows a page holds depends on the screen: `ui:layout` measures the list with the same `children` first, and the rows per page and page count go to both the list and the pager, so the count stays right in landscape and on other devices. The buy button is `enabled = false` when money is short, and the money label has a `reserve` so the title does not move when the number changes. Every value lives in the script and is passed in every frame.

## Full page: confirm dialog

```lua widget=page_dialog
-- S (size table) and F (fonts) are defined once per file; see "Quick start"

-- State (top of the file)
local open = true

local function draw_page_behind(g)
  local w, h = g:size()
  local x, y = S.margin, S.margin
  g:text(x, y, "Chapter 3 · Return", { font = F.title, bold = true })
  y = y + F.title.line_height + S.lg
  local line = F.body.line_height + S.sm
  for i = 0, (h - y) // line - 1 do
    local width = i % 4 == 3 and (w - 2 * x) * 3 // 5 or w - 2 * x   -- a short last line per paragraph, like body text
    g:rect(x, y + i * line + (line - S.sm) // 2, width, S.sm, { fill = true })
  end
  g:pattern(0, 0, w, h, { kind = "dot", density = 50, color = 0 })
end

-- on_draw, between ui:begin_frame(g) and ui:end_frame()
local W, H = g:size()
draw_page_behind(g)
if open then
  -- a full-screen stack centres the dialog: no coordinates change in landscape or on another size
  ui:stack("dim", { x = 0, y = 0, w = W, h = H, padding = S.xl, children = {
    { kind = "column", w = "100%", max_w = S.dialog_w, h = "fit", justify_self = "center", align_self = "center",
      background = 0, border = true, radius = S.radius_lg, line_width = S.line, padding = S.lg, gap = S.md, children = {
      { kind = "label", id = "d_t", text = "Delete this note?", font = F.title, bold = true, h = "fit" },
      { kind = "label", id = "d_b", text = "This cannot be undone", font = F.body, h = "fit" },
      { kind = "row", gap = S.md, children = {
        { kind = "button", id = "no", text = "Cancel", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius },
        { kind = "button", id = "yes", text = "Delete", grow = 1, h = S.control, radius = S.radius, emphasis = true },
      } },
    } },
  } })
end

-- on_input, after local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev)
if action == "activate" and (id == "yes" or id == "no") then open = false end
```

Draw the underlying page first, cover it with white dots via `g:pattern` to dim it, and then draw a white `column` with a frame. The dialog is `"100%"` wide capped by `max_w = S.dialog_w`, and the stack's `padding = S.xl` keeps space around it: it fills a narrow screen and does not stretch on a wide one. While it is open, declare only the dialog's widgets so the arrow keys cannot reach the page underneath; if the page has widgets of its own, give the dialog a second UI object (another `ctx.ui:create()` call), and the page's focus stays put when the dialog closes. For a simple confirmation, you can also use the system dialog `ctx.dialog`.

## Draw it yourself: sizes and recipes

Use `g` to draw what the UI library does not provide. The sections below record the sizes and drawing code of the **device's own system screens**, so your screens can match them. Always get fonts with `ctx.fonts:size(px)`.

These are reference values measured on the X4 system screens, and they follow different rules from your own app:

| | System reference values (sections below) | Your own app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lengths | Pixels as measured, such as a row height of `58` or a menu width of `265` | `S.*` values from the "Size table"; control heights from the font's line height |
| Positions | Formulas in `W` and `H`, with the X4 portrait (480×800) value in parentheses for checking | Containers or `ui:layout`; when drawing yourself, `W - S.margin - width` for the right edge, `H - height` for the bottom, `(W - width) // 2` to centre |
| Text | The system default size | Position with `align` / `valign`; measure width with `font:measure` instead of estimating from the character count |

Use these values when you copy the look of a particular system control; when in doubt, use the size table. When several elements sit side by side, let `ui:layout` compute their boxes first, then draw inside them.

## Draw it: Bluetooth keyboard (2.10)

A Bluetooth keyboard that the user paired in system settings works without any work from the app: the arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Enter, Esc, and Backspace arrive as ordinary keys (`up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` `back`), and while the docked keyboard or text entry is open, the user types directly. The app doesn't receive the other keys.

To get every key (shortcuts, typing games, terminals), call `ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })`. Every launch starts without listening; you can call it while no keyboard is connected, and it takes effect once one connects.

```lua
local line = ""

function on_start(ctx)
  ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.source == "keyboard" then
    if ev.phase ~= "up" and ev.text then line = line .. ev.text end
    if ev.phase ~= "up" and ev.code == "Backspace" then line = line:sub(1, -2) end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | `"keyboard"`. Events from the device keys or a page turner don't have this field |
| `key` | The arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Enter, and Esc are still `up` … `back`; every other key, Backspace included, is `"other"` |
| `code` | The key position, the same as the browser's `KeyboardEvent.code`, for example `KeyA`, `Digit1`, `Backspace` |
| `text` | The character typed on a US layout with Shift applied; present only on `down` and `repeat`, and absent while Ctrl, Alt, or Meta is held |
| `mods` | `{ shift, ctrl, alt, meta }` |
| `phase` | `down`, `repeat` (sent repeatedly while held), `up` |

Once listening, Backspace no longer acts as back; Esc and the device's back key still do. Tell the user on screen which keys do something, because most users have no keyboard at hand: the keyboard is an extra way to operate the app, and the arrow keys and touch must still cover the whole app.

## Design rules: UI on e-ink

| Rule | How |
| --- | --- |
| Black and white only | Normal frames use only paper 0 and ink 15. A container `background` is rendered as dots: 0–2 is paper, 3–7 light dots, 8–12 dark dots, 13–15 ink. Dots break up strokes, small text especially, so keep text on paper and use dots only for blocks or frames (see "Layout: stacks and shades") |
| Hierarchy through size and weight | Separate levels with `ctx.fonts:size(px)` (for example 40 / 30 / 24 / 20) and set `bold = true` on titles; do not rely on grey text |
| Stable digits | Use `tabular = true` for clocks, scores, and countdowns; add `reserve` to `w = "fit"` numbers so the width fits the widest value |
| One primary action | Each screen has one `emphasis` button; the others are outlined |
| Current item | Use `selected` (inverted) for the current item in menus and grids; for top tabs, use the lighter `selected_style = "underline"` |
| Leave refresh to the system | Opening a new screen, switching tabs, paging a list, moving focus, flipping a switch: always plain `ctx:invalidate()`. Do not call `ctx:invalidate("full")`; it makes every tap flash the whole screen black, and the system already clears ghosting with periodic automatic full refreshes |
| No animation | A frame takes about 0.5 s, so do not draw a pressed state or transitions; the next frame is the feedback for a tap |
| Size and position | Read the screen size every frame with `g:size()`; never hard-code 480×800. Let `ui:column` / `ui:row` / `ui:grid` / `ui:stack` or `ui:layout` place things instead of computing coordinates; take lengths only from the `S.*` entries of the "Size table", and derive control heights from the font |
| Spacing shows grouping | `S.xs` / `S.sm` inside a group, `S.md` between controls, `S.lg` between groups; `S.margin` for the page margin |
| Hit areas | Every tappable element is at least `S.hit` (44) square; one-line controls at `S.control` height already meet this |
| Keyboard area | On pages with input fields, reserve the bottom `ctx.input.keyboard_h` pixels for the system keyboard |
| Two devices | Every screen must be fully usable with the arrow keys + `ok` (X4 Classic) and by tapping (X4 Pro). Do not branch on the device model; check `ctx.input.pointer` instead |
| Text width | The user chooses the typeface, so always measure text width (`font:measure`) and never estimate it from the character count; when text does not fit, use `font_min` or an ellipsis |
